# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — PTP Header Structure in C

<!-- source: 037_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2101–2110 -->

```
typedef struct ETHER_PACKET { char  dst_addr[6];             //destination address char  src_addr[6];             //source address char  length[2];               //length of actual data char  data[DATA_SIZE];         //application data char  fdlimit[DELIMIT_SIZE];   //32-bit delimit (if manual appending) char  fcs[4];                  //crc frame checksum, used by RX buffer. } ETHER_PACKET;
```

## PTP Header Structure in C

The following code is an example of the PTP message format.

```
/* PTP Message Format (Refer to PTP Frame Over IPv4)*/ typedef struct EMAC_PTP_HEADER { unsigned char    messageType:4,    //PTP Version 2 message type transportSpecific:4; unsigned char    versionPTP;       //PTP Version (1 or 2) unsigned short    messageLength; unsigned char    domainNumber; unsigned char    RESERVED1; unsigned short    flagField; unsigned char    correctionField[8]; unsigned char    RESERVED2[4]; unsigned char    sourcePortIdentity[10]; unsigned short    sequenceid; unsigned char    controlField;     //PTP Version 1 message type unsigned char    logMessageInterval; }EMAC_PTP_HEADER;
```

## ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions

RGMII, RMII, MII Ethernet Controller (EMAC) contains the following registers.

Table 30-112: ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register List

| Name                  | Description                                                       |
|-----------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|
| EMAC_DMA[n]_CTL       | DMAChannel n Control Register                                     |
| EMAC_DMA[n]_RXBUF_CUR | DMAChannel n Current Application Receive Buffer Address Register  |
| EMAC_DMA[n]_RXDSC_CUR | DMAChannel n Current Application Receive Descriptor Register      |
| EMAC_DMA[n]_TXBUF_CUR | DMAChannel n Current Application Transmit Buffer Address Register |
| EMAC_DMA[n]_TXDSC_CUR | DMAChannel n Current Application Transmit Descriptor Register     |
| EMAC_DMA[n]_IEN       | DMAChannel n Interrupt Enable Register                            |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — DMA Channel n Control Register

<!-- source: 038_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2111–2112 -->

## DMA Channel n Control Register

The EMAC\_DMA[n]\_CTL register specifies the MSS value for segmentation, length to skip between two descriptors, and also the features such as header splitting and 8xPBL mode.

Figure 30-58: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_CTL Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-113: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_CTL Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
|--------------------|------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 24 (R/W)           | SPH        | Split Headers. When the EMAC_DMA[n]_CTL.SPH bit is set (=1), the DMAsplits the header and payload in the receive path. The DMAwrites the header to Buffer Address1 of RDES0. The DMAwrites the payload to the buffer to which the Buffer Address2 is pointing. The software must ensure that the header fits into the receive buffers. If the header length exceeds the receive buffer size, the DMAdoes not split the header and payload. The EMAC_DMA[n]_CTL.SPH bit is available only when the split header feature is enabled (EMAC_HW_FTR_PSNT1.SPHEN =1). 0 Split Headers Feature is Disabled |
| 20:18 (R/W)        | DSL        | Descriptor Skip Length. The EMAC_DMA[n]_CTL.DSL bit specifies the number of 32-bit words to skip be- tween two unchained descriptors. The address skipping starts from the end of the cur- rent descriptor to the start of the next descriptor. When EMAC_DMA[n]_CTL.DSL = 0, the DMAtakes the descriptor table as con- tiguous.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

Table 30-113: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_CTL Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|--------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 16 (R/W)           | PBLX8      | 8xPBL Mode. When the EMAC_DMA[n]_CTL.PBLX8 bit is set, the PBL value programmed in bits[21:16] in EMAC_DMA[n]_TXCTL and bits[21:16] in EMAC_DMA[n]_RXCTL is multiplied by eight times. Therefore, the DMAtransfers the data in 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, and 256 beats depending on the PBL value. 0 8xPBL Mode is Disabled                                   |
| 13:0 (R/W)         | MSS        | Maximum Segment Size. The EMAC_DMA[n]_CTL.MSS field specifies the maximum segment size to be used while segmenting the packet. The EMAC_DMA[n]_CTL.MSS field is valid only when EMAC_DMA[n]_TXCTL.TSE =1. The value programmed in this field must be more than the configured data width in bytes. Use a EMAC_DMA[n]_CTL.MSS value of 64 bytes or more. |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — DMA Channel n Receive Descriptor List Address Register

<!-- source: 045_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2122–2122 -->

## DMA Channel n Receive Descriptor List Address Register

The EMAC\_DMA[n]\_RXDSC\_ADDR register points the DMA to the start of the receive descriptor list.

The descriptor lists reside in the physical memory space of the application. It must be 32-bit aligned. The DMA internally converts it to bus width aligned address by making the corresponding least significant bits low.

Writing to the EMAC\_DMA[n]\_RXDSC\_ADDR register is permitted only when reception is stopped. When stopped, this register must be written to before the receive start command is given.

Write to this register only when Rx DMA has stopped (EMAC\_DMA[n]\_RXCTL.SR = 0). When stopped, this register can be written with a new descriptor list address.

When EMAC\_DMA[n]\_RXCTL.SR = 1, the DMA takes the newly programmed descriptor base address.

Figure 30-65: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_RXDSC\_ADDR Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-120: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_RXDSC\_ADDR Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|--------------------|------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:2 (R/W)         | RDESLA     | Start of Receive List. The EMAC_DMA[n]_RXDSC_ADDR.RDESLA field contains the base address of the first descriptor in the Rx descriptor list. The DMAignores the last two bits (1:0) and internally takes these bits as all-zero. Therefore, these LSB bits are read-only (RO). |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — DMA Channel n Receive Control Register

<!-- source: 047_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2124–2126 -->

## DMA Channel n Receive Control Register

The EMAC\_DMA[n]\_RXCTL register controls the Rx features such as PBL, buffer size, and extended status.

Figure 30-67: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_RXCTL Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-122: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_RXCTL Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
|--------------------|------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31 (R/W)           | RPF        | Rx Packet Flush. The EMAC_DMA[n]_RXCTL.RPF bit enables the Rx packet flush feature. When set (= 1), the EMAC module automatically flushes the packet from the Rx queues desig- nated to this DMARx channel, when it is stopped. When the EMAC_DMA[n]_RXCTL.RPF bit remains set and the DMAis restarted by the soft- ware driver, the packets residing in the Rx queues that were received when this RxDMA was stopped, are flushed out. The packets that are received by the MAC after the RxDMA is restarted are routed to the RxDMA. The flushing is done on the read side of the Rx queue. When the EMAC_DMA[n]_RXCTL.RPF bit is cleared (= 0), the EMAC module does not flush the packet in the Rx queue destined to this RxDMA channel when it is in STOP state. This operation can cause head-of-line blocking in the corresponding Rx queue. Note: The stopping of packet flow from a Rx DMAchannel to the application by set- ting RPF works only when there is one-to-one mapping of Rx queue to RxDMA channels. In dynamic mapping mode, setting this bit can flush packets from unintend- ed Rx queues which are destined to the stopped Rx DMAchannel. Disabled |
| 31 (R/W)           |            | 0 Rx Packet Flush is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| 31 (R/W)           |            | 1 Rx Packet Flush is Enabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

Table 30-122: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_RXCTL Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|--------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 21:16 (R/W)        | RXPBL      | Receive Programmable Burst Length. The EMAC_DMA[n]_RXCTL.RXPBL field indicates the maximum number of beats to be transferred in one DMAblock data transfer. The DMAalways attempts max burst as specified in PBL each time it starts a burst transfer on the application bus. Program PBL with any of the following values: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, or 32. Any other value results in undefined behavior. To transfer more than 32 beats, perform the following steps: 1. Set the 8xPBL mode in the EMAC_DMA[n]_CTL register. 2. Set the RxPBL. Note: The maximum value of RxPBL must be less than or equal to half the Rx queue size (EMAC_RQ[n]_OPMODE.RQS) in terms of beats. This is required so that the Rx queue has space to store at least another Rx PBL worth of data while the RxDMA is transferring a block of data. For example, in the total locations in Rx queue of size 512 bytes is 128, so RxPBL and 8xPBL needs to be programmed to less than or equal to 64. |
| 14:3 (R/W)         | RBSZ_13_Y  | Receive Buffer Size High. RBSZ[13:0] is split into two fields: higher EMAC_DMA[n]_RXCTL.RBSZ_13_Y and lower RBSZ_x_0. The RBSZ[13:0] field indicates the size of the Rx buffers speci- fied in bytes. The maximum buffer size is limited to 16K bytes. The buffer size is ap- plicable to payload buffers when split headers are enabled. Note: The buffer size must be a multiple of 4 bytes. This is required even if the value of buffer address pointer is not aligned to data bus width. Hence, the lower RBSZ_x_0 bits are read-only and the value is considered as all-zero. Thus, the EMAC_DMA[n]_RXCTL.RBSZ_13_Y indicates the buffer size in terms of loca- tions (with the width same as bus width).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| 2:1 (R/NW)         | RBSZ_X_0   | Receive Buffer Size Low. RBSZ[13:0] is split into two fields RBSZ_13_y and RBSZ_x_0. The EMAC_DMA[n]_RXCTL.RBSZ_X_0 field is the lower field whose width is based on data bus width of the configuration. The EMAC_DMA[n]_RXCTL.RBSZ_X_0 field is 2 bits wide. The EMAC_DMA[n]_RXCTL.RBSZ_X_0 field is read-only (RO).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

|--------------------|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 0 (R/W)            | SR         | Start or Stop Receive. When the EMAC_DMA[n]_RXCTL.SR bit is set (=1), the DMAtries to acquire the descriptor from the receive list and processes the incoming packets. The DMAtries to acquire descriptor from either of the following positions: The current position in the list - This is the address set by the EMAC_DMA[n]_RXDSC_ADDR register. The position at which the Rx process was previously stopped - If the DMAdoes not own the current descriptor, the reception is suspended and the EMAC_DMA[n]_STAT.RBU bit is set (=1). The start receive command is effective only when the reception is stopped. If the com- mand is issued before configuring the EMAC_DMA[n]_RXDSC_ADDR register, the DMAbehavior is unpredictable. When EMAC_DMA[n]_RXCTL.SR bit = 0, the Rx DMAoperation is stopped after the transfer of the current packet. The next descriptor position in the receive list is saved, and it becomes the current position after the Rx process is restarted. The stop receive command is effective only when the Rx process is in the running (waiting for Rx packet) or suspended state. 0 Stop Receive |
| 0 (R/W)            |            | 1 Start Receive                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| 0 (R/W)            |            |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — DMA Channel n Extended Receive Control Register

## DMA Channel n Extended Receive Control Register

The EMAC\_DMA[n]\_RXCTL2 register controls the Rx features such as Rx descriptor ring length and alternate Rx buffer size.

Figure 30-68: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_RXCTL2 Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
|--------------------|------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 23:16 (R/W)        | ARBS       | Alternate Receive Buffer Size. The EMAC_DMA[n]_RXCTL2.ARBS field indicates the size in bytes for buffer 1, when programmed to a non-zero value (when the split header feature is not enabled). When the split header feature is enabled, the EMAC_DMA[n]_RXCTL2.ARBS field indicates the buffer size for header data. The maximum alternate buffer is limited to 1020 bytes for the 32-bit data bus width. When EMAC_DMA[n]_RXCTL2.ARBS = 0, the Rx Buffer1 and Rx Buffer2 sizes are based on EMAC_DMA[n]_RXCTL.RBSZ. |
| 9:0 (R/W)          | RDRL       | Receive Descriptor Ring Length. The EMAC_DMA[n]_RXCTL2 register sets the maximum number of Rx descriptors in the circular descriptor ring. The maximum number of descriptors is limited to 1K descriptors. For example, program any value up to 0x3FF in this field. The EMAC_DMA[n]_RXCTL2.RDRL field is 10 bits wide. When programming 0x3FF, there are 1024 descriptors. For 10 descriptors, program it to a value of 0x9.                                                                                         |

## DMA Channel n Receive Interrupt Watchdog Timer Register

The EMAC\_DMA[n]\_RXINTWDTMR register indicates the watchdog timeout for Receive Interrupt (RI) from the DMA. When this register is written with a non-zero value, it enables the watchdog timer for the EMAC\_DMA[n]\_STAT.RI bit.

<!-- image -->

RWTU (R/W)

Count Units Receive Interrupt Watchdog Timer

Figure 30-69: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_RXINTWDTMR Register Diagram

Table 30-124: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_RXINTWDTMR Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
|--------------------|------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 17:16 (R/W)        | RWTU       | Receive Interrupt Watchdog Timer Count Units. The EMAC_DMA[n]_RXINTWDTMR.RWTU field indicates the number of SCLK0 cycles corresponding to one unit in the EMAC_DMA[n]_RXINTWDTMR.RWT field. For example, when EMAC_DMA[n]_RXINTWDTMR.RWT =2 and EMAC_DMA[n]_RXINTWDTMR.RWTU = 1, the watchdog timer is configured for 2 * 512 = 1024 SCLK0 cycles. 0 256 1 512 2 1024 |
| 17:16 (R/W)        | RWTU       | 3 2048                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| 17:16 (R/W)        | RWTU       |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| 17:16 (R/W)        | RWTU       |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| 17:16 (R/W)        | RWTU       |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

Table 30-124: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_RXINTWDTMR Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|--------------------|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 7:0 (R/W)          | RWT        | Receive Interrupt Watchdog Timer Count. The EMAC_DMA[n]_RXINTWDTMR.RWT field indicates the number of SCLK0 cy- cles, multiplied by factor indicated in EMAC_DMA[n]_RXINTWDTMR.RWTU field, for which the watchdog timer is set. The watchdog timer is triggered with the programmed value after the Rx DMAcom- pletes the transfer of a packet for which EMAC_DMA[n]_STAT.RI = 0 register, be- cause of the setting of Interrupt Enable bit in the corresponding descriptor RDES3[30]. When the watchdog timer runs out, the RI bit is set and the timer is stopped. The watchdog timer is reset when the RI bit is set (=1) because of automatic setting of RI as per the Interrupt Enable bit RDES3[30] of any received packet. |

## DMA Channel n Slot Function Control and Status register

The EMAC\_DMA[n]\_SFN\_CTLSTAT register contains the control bits for slot function and the status for transmit path.

It is used for slot comparison.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| 15:4 (R/W)         | SIV        | Slot Interval Value. The EMAC_DMA[n]_SFN_CTLSTAT.SIV field controls the period of the slot in- terval in which the TxDMA fetches the scheduled packets. A value of 0 specifies the slot interval of 1 us while the maximum value 4095 specifies the slot interval of 4096us. The default/reset value is 0x07C which corresponds to a slot interval of 125 us.                                             |

The software driver (application) reads the EMAC\_DMA[n]\_STAT register during interrupt service routine or polling to determine the status of the DMA.

Bit 21 -- 1'b1: Error during data transfer by RxDMA -- 1'b0: No Error during data transfer by RxDMA Bit 20 -- 1'b1: Error during descriptor access -- 1'b0: Error during data buffer access Bit 19 -- 1'b1: Error during read transfer -- 1'b0: Error during write transfer The EMAC_DMA[n]_STAT.REB field is valid only when the FBE bit is set. It does not generate an interrupt. |

It does not generate an interrupt.    |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — DMA Channel n Transmit Descriptor List Address Register

<!-- source: 052_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2139–2139 -->

## DMA Channel n Transmit Descriptor List Address Register

The EMAC\_DMA[n]\_TXDSC\_ADDR register points the DMA to the start of transmit descriptor list. The descriptor lists reside in the physical memory space of the application and must be 32-bit aligned. The DMA internally converts it to bus width aligned address by making the corresponding LSB to low.

Write to the EMAC\_DMA[n]\_TXDSC\_ADDR register only when the Tx DMA has stopped (EMAC\_DMA[n]\_TXCTL.ST = 0). When stopped, this register can be written with a new descriptor list address. When EMAC\_DMA[n]\_TXCTL.ST = 1, the DMA takes the newly-programmed descriptor base address. If this register is not changed when EMAC\_DMA[n]\_TXCTL.ST = 0, the DMA takes the descriptor address where it was stopped earlier.

Figure 30-72: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_TXDSC\_ADDR Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-127: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_TXDSC\_ADDR Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|--------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:2 (R/W)         | TDESLA     | Start of Transmit List. The EMAC_DMA[n]_TXDSC_ADDR.TDESLA field contains the base address of the first descriptor in the transmit descriptor list. The DMAignores the LSB bits (1:0) and internally takes these bits as all-zero. Therefore, these LSB bits are read-only (RO). |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — DMA Channel n Transmit Descriptor Ring Length Register

<!-- source: 053_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2140–2140 -->

## DMA Channel n Transmit Descriptor Ring Length Register

The EMAC\_DMA[n]\_TXDSC\_RLEN register contains the length of the transmit descriptor ring.

Figure 30-73: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_TXDSC\_RLEN Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-128: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_TXDSC\_RLEN Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|--------------------|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 9:0 (R/W)          | TDRL       | Transmit Descriptor Ring Length. The EMAC_DMA[n]_TXDSC_RLEN.TDRL field sets the maximum number of Tx descriptors in the circular descriptor ring. The maximum number of descriptors is lim- ited to 1K descriptors. A minimum ring descriptor length of 4 is recommended. For example, program any value up to 0x3FF in this field. The EMAC_DMA[n]_TXDSC_RLEN.TDRL field is 10 bits wide. To program 0x3FF, 1024 descriptors are available. For 10 descriptors, program it to a value of 0x9. |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — DMA Channel n Transmit Descriptor Tail Pointer Register

<!-- source: 054_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2141–2141 -->

## DMA Channel n Transmit Descriptor Tail Pointer Register

The EMAC\_DMA[n]\_TXDSC\_TLPTR register points to an offset from the base and indicates the location of the last valid descriptor.

Figure 30-74: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_TXDSC\_TLPTR Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-129: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_TXDSC\_TLPTR Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|--------------------|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:2 (R/W)         | TDTP       | Transmit Descriptor Tail Pointer. The EMAC_DMA[n]_TXDSC_TLPTR.TDTP field contains the tail pointer for the Tx descriptor ring. The software writes the tail pointer to add more descriptors to the Tx channel. The hardware tries to transmit all packets referenced by the descriptors be- tween the head and the tail pointer registers. |

## DMA Channel n Transmit Control Register

The EMAC\_DMA[n]\_TXCTL register controls the Tx features such as PBL, TCP segmentation, and Tx channel weights.

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|--------------------|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 30:29 (R/W)        | TFSEL      | TBS Fetch Select. The EMAC_DMA[n]_TXCTL.TFSEL field select the EMAC_DMA_TBS_CTRL0 - EMAC_DMA_TBS_CTRL3 register fields (FTOS, FGSN, FTOV) for the channel.                                                                                                                                                   |
| 30:29 (R/W)        | TFSEL      | 0 EMAC_DMA_TBS_CTL0                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| 30:29 (R/W)        | TFSEL      | 1 EMAC_DMA_TBS_CTL1                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| 30:29 (R/W)        | TFSEL      | 2 EMAC_DMA_TBS_CTL2                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| 30:29 (R/W)        | TFSEL      | 3 EMAC_DMA_TBS_CTL3                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| 28 (R/W)           | EDSE       | Enhanced Descriptor Enable. When EMAC_DMA[n]_TXCTL.EDSE = 1, the corresponding channel uses en- hanced descriptors that are 32 bytes for both normal and context descriptors. When cleared (=0), the corresponding channel uses the descriptors that are 16 bytes. 0 Enhanced Descriptor is Disabled Enabled |
| 28 (R/W)           | EDSE       | 1 Enhanced Descriptor is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| 28 (R/W)           | EDSE       |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

Table 30-130: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_TXCTL Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|--------------------|------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 21:16 (R/W)        | TXPBL      | Transmit Programmable Burst Length. The EMAC_DMA[n]_TXCTL.TXPBL field indicates the maximum number of beats to be transferred in one DMAblock data transfer. The DMAalways attempts max burst as specified in PBL each time it starts a burst transfer on the application bus. Program PBL with any of the following values: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, or 32. Any other value results in undefined behavior. To transfer more than 32 beats, perform the following steps: 1. Set the 8xPBL mode in EMAC_DMA[n]_CTL register. 2. Set the TxPBL. Note: The maximum value of TxPBL must be less than or equal to half the Tx queue size (EMAC_TQ[n]_OPMODE.TQS) in terms of beats. This is required so that the Tx queue has space to store at least another Tx PBL worth of data while the MTL Tx queue controller is transferring data to MAC. For example, in 64-bit data width con- figurations the total locations in Tx queue of size 512 bytes is 64, TxPBL and 8xPBL must be programmed to less than or equal to 32. |
| 15 (R/W)           | IPBL       | Ignore PBL Requirement. When EMAC_DMA[n]_TXCTL.IPBL = 1, the DMAdoes not check for PBL num- ber of locations in the MTL before initiating a transfer. If space is not available, the MTL can use handshaking to slow the DMA. Note: The EMAC_DMA[n]_TXCTL.IPBL bit/mode must not be used when multi- ple transmit DMAchannels are enabled as it might block other transmit and receive DMAchannels from accessing the read data channel of SCB bus until space is availa- ble in transmit queue for the current transfer.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| 15 (R/W)           | IPBL       | 0 Ignore PBL Requirement is Disabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| 15 (R/W)           | IPBL       | 1 Ignore PBL Requirement is Enabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| 14:13 (R/W)        | TSE_MODE   | TSE Mode. The EMAC_DMA[n]_TXCTL.TSE_MODE field indicates the TSE mode.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| 14:13 (R/W)        | TSE_MODE   | 0 TSO/USO. Segmentation functionality is enabled.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| 14:13 (R/W)        | TSE_MODE   | 1 UFO with Checksum. Enables the UDP fragmentation functionality with checksum for all the UDP packets.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| 14:13 (R/W)        | TSE_MODE   | 2 UFO Without Checksum. Enables the UDP fragmenta- tion functionality without Checksum for all the UDP packets.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| 14:13 (R/W)        | TSE_MODE   | 3 Reserved                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|--------------------|------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 12 (R/W)           | TSE        | TCP Segmentation Enabled. When EMAC_DMA[n]_TXCTL.TSE = 1, the DMAperforms the TCP segmenta- tion or UDP segmentation/fragmentation for packets in this channel. The TCP seg- mentation or UDP packet's segmentation/fragmentation is done only for those packets for which the TSE bit (TDES0[19]) is set in the Tx Normal descriptor. When EMAC_DMA[n]_TXCTL.TSE = 1, the TxPBL value must be greater than 4. 0 TCP Segmentation is Disabled |
| 4 (R/W)            | OSF        | Operate on Second Packet. When EMAC_DMA[n]_TXCTL.OSF = 1, the DMAprocesses the second packet of the transmit data, even before the status for the first packet is obtained.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| 3:1 (R/W)          | TCW        | Transmit Channel Weight. The EMAC_DMA[n]_TXCTL.TCW field indicates the weight assigned to the corre- sponding transmit channel. When reset is complete, EMAC_DMA[n]_TXCTL.TCW = 0 for all channels by default, resulting in equal weights to all channels.                                                                                                                                                                                    |

Table 30-130: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_TXCTL Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
|--------------------|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 0 (R/W)            | ST         | Start or Stop Transmission Command. When the EMAC_DMA[n]_TXCTL.ST bit is set, transmission is placed in the run- ning state. The DMAchecks the transmit list at the current position for a packet to be transmitted. The DMAtries to acquire descriptor from either of the following positions: The current position in the list - This is the base address of the transmit list configured by the EMAC_DMA[n]_TXDSC_ADDR register. The position at which the transmission was previously stopped - If the DMAdoes not own the current descriptor, the transmission enters the suspended state and the EMAC_DMA[n]_STAT.TBU =1. The start transmission command is effective only when the transmission is stopped. If the command is issued before configuring the EMAC_DMA[n]_TXDSC_ADDR register, the DMAbehavior is unpredictable. When EMAC_DMA[n]_TXCTL.ST = 0, the transmission process is placed in the stopped state after completing the transmission of the current packet. The Next De- scriptor position in the transmit list is saved, and it becomes the current position when the transmission is restarted. To change the list address, program EMAC_DMA[n]_TXDSC_ADDR register with a new value when EMAC_DMA[n]_TXCTL.ST = 0. The new value is considered when EMAC_DMA[n]_TXCTL.ST =1 again. The stop transmission command is ef- fective only when the transmission of the current packet is complete or the transmis- sion is in the suspended state. 0 Stop Transmission Command |
| 0 (R/W)            |            | 1 Start Transmission Command                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
