# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — DMA Mode Register

<!-- source: 060_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2159–2161 -->

## DMA Mode Register

The EMAC\_DMA\_MODE register establishes the bus operating modes for the DMA.

Figure 30-80: EMAC\_DMA\_MODE Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-135: EMAC\_DMA\_MODE Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|--------------------|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 17:16 (R/W)        | INTM       | Interrupt Mode. The EMAC_DMA_MODE.INTM field defines the interrupt mode of the EMAC mod- ule. The behavior of the following outputs change depending on the following settings: - EMAC_DMA[n]_TX (Transmit Per Channel Interrupt) - EMAC_DMA[n]_RX (Receive Per Channel Interrupt) - EMAC_STAT (Common Interrupt) It also changes the behavior of the EMAC_DMA[n]_STAT.RI and EMAC_DMA[n]_STAT.TI bits. - 00: EMAC_DMA[n]_TX/RX are pulse signals for each TX/RX packet transfer com- pletion events (irrespective of whether corresponding interrupts are enabled) for which IOC bits are enabled in descriptor. EMAC_STAT is also asserted when corresponding interrupts are enabled and cleared only when software clears the corresponding RI/TI status bits. - 01: EMAC_DMA[n]_TX/RX are level signals asserted on TX/RX packet transfer completion event when corresponding interrupts are enabled and deasserted when the software clears the corresponding RI/TI status bits. The EMAC_STAT is not asserted for these TX/RX packet transfer completion events. - 10: EMAC_DMA[n]_TX/RX are level signals asserted on TX/RX packet transfer completion event when corresponding interrupts are enabled and deasserted when the software clears the corresponding RI/TI status bits. However, the signal is asserted again if the same event occurred again before it was cleared. The EMAC_STAT is not asserted for these TX/RX packet transfer completion events. - 11: Reserved For more details, see Transfer Complete Interrupt Behavior. 0 See Above Description 1 See Above Description 2 See Above Description |
| 11 (R/W)           | TXPR       | Transmit Priority. When set, the EMAC_DMA_MODE.TXPR bit indicates that the Tx DMAhas higher priority than the Rx DMAduring arbitration for the system-side bus. 0 Transmit Priority is Disabled 1 Transmit Priority is Enabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

Table 30-135: EMAC\_DMA\_MODE Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name     | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
|--------------------|--------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 8 (R/W)            | DSPW         | Descriptor Posted Write. When the EMAC_DMA_MODE.DSPW bit is cleared (=0), it indicates that the descrip- tor writes are always non-posted. When set (=1), the EMAC_DMA_MODE.DSPW bit indicates that the descriptor is non-posted only when the IOC (Interrupt on Comple- tion) is set in last descriptor. Otherwise, the descriptor writes are always posted.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Descriptor Posted Write. When the EMAC_DMA_MODE.DSPW bit is cleared (=0), it indicates that the descrip- tor writes are always non-posted. When set (=1), the EMAC_DMA_MODE.DSPW bit indicates that the descriptor is non-posted only when the IOC (Interrupt on Comple- tion) is set in last descriptor. Otherwise, the descriptor writes are always posted.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| 8 (R/W)            | DSPW         | 0                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Disable                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| 8 (R/W)            | DSPW         | 1                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Enable                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| 4:2 (R/W)          | TAA          | Transmit Arbitration Algorithm. The EMAC_DMA_MODE.TAA field is used to select the arbitration algorithm for the transmit side when multiple Tx DMAs are selected.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Transmit Arbitration Algorithm. The EMAC_DMA_MODE.TAA field is used to select the arbitration algorithm for the transmit side when multiple Tx DMAs are selected.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| 4:2 (R/W)          | TAA          | 0                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Fixed Priority (Channel 0 Has the Lowest Priority and the Last Channel Has the Highest Priority)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

The EMAC\_DMA\_SYSBMODE register controls the behavior of the SPB or SCB requester. It mainly controls burst splitting and number of outstanding requests.

| 19:16 (R/W)        | RD_OSR_LMT | SCB Maximum Read Outstanding Request Limit. This value limits the maximum outstanding request on the SCB read interface. Maxi- mum outstanding requests = EMAC_DMA_SYSBMODE.RD_OSR_LMT + 1.  |
| 13 (R/W)           | ONEKBBE    | 1 KB Boundary Crossing Enable. The EMAC_DMA_SYSBMODE.ONEKBBE bit indicates whether the burst transfers performed by the SCB requester do not cross a 1 KB or (the default) 4 KB boundary.    |

| 13 (R/W)           | ONEKBBE    | 1 Enable                                                                                                                                                                                     |

When the EMAC_DMA_SYSBMODE.AAL = 0, the SCB or SPB requester performs burst transfers on read and write channels without aligning to address boundaries. |

Offset is Invalid |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — LPI One Microsecond Tic Counter Register

<!-- source: 066_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2169–2169 -->

## LPI One Microsecond Tic Counter Register

The EMAC\_ONEUS\_TIC\_CNT register controls the generation of the reference time (1 microsecond tic) for all of the LPI timers. This timer has to be programmed by the software initially.

Figure 30-86: EMAC\_ONEUS\_TIC\_CNT Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-141: EMAC\_ONEUS\_TIC\_CNT Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name     | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|--------------------|--------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 11:0 (R/W)         | TIC_1US_CNTR | 1US TIC Counter. The application must program the EMAC_ONEUS_TIC_CNT.TIC_1US_CNTR field so that the number of clock cycles of SCLK0 is 1us. (Subtract 1 from the value before programming). For example, if the SCLK0 is 100MHz, this field must be pro- grammed to value 100 - 1 = 99 (which is 0x63). This is required to generate the 1 us events that are used to update some of the EEE-related counters. |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — MAC Address 0 High Register

<!-- source: 068_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2171–2171 -->

## MAC Address 0 High Register

The EMAC\_ADDR0\_HI register holds the upper 16 bits of the first 6-byte MAC address of the station. The first DA byte that is received on the (G)MII interface corresponds to the LS byte (Bits [7:0]) of the EMAC\_ADDR0\_LO register. For example, if 0x112233445566 is received (0x11 in lane 0 of the first column) on the (G)MII as the destination address, then the MAC Address 0 Register [47:0] is compared with 0x665544332211.

The MAC address registers are configured to be double-synchronized to the (G)MII clock domains. Hence, the synchronization is triggered only when bits[31:24] (in little endian mode) or bits[7:0] (in big endian mode) of the EMAC\_ADDR0\_LO register are written. For proper synchronization updates, the consecutive writes to this register should be performed only after at least four clock cycles in the (G)MII clock domain.

Figure 30-88: EMAC\_ADDR0\_HI Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-143: EMAC\_ADDR0\_HI Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
|--------------------|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31 (R/NW)          | AE         | Address Enable. The EMAC_ADDR0_HI.AE bit is always set (=1).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| 23:16 (R/W)        | DCS        | DMAChannel Select. When EMAC_MAC_EXT_CFG.PDC = 0, the EMAC_ADDR0_HI.DCS field con- tains the binary representation of the DMAchannel number to which an Rx packet whose DA matches the MAC Address 0 content is routed. When EMAC_MAC_EXT_CFG.PDC = 1, the EMAC_ADDR0_HI.DCS field con- tains the one-hot representation of one or more DMAchannel numbers to which an Rx packet whose DA matches the MAC Address 0 content is routed. |
| 15:0 (R/W)         | ADDRHI     | MAC address 0[47:32]. The EMAC_ADDR0_HI.ADDRHI field contains the upper 16 bits [47:32] of the first 6-byte MAC address. The MAC uses this field for filtering the received packets and inserting the MAC address in the Transmit Flow Control (Pause) Packets.                                                                                                                                                                        |

## MAC Address n High Register

The EMAC\_ADDR[i]\_HI register holds the upper 16 bits of the second 6-byte MAC address of the station.

If the MAC address registers are configured to be double-synchronized to the (G)MII clock domains, the synchronization is triggered only when Bits[31:24] (in little-endian mode) or bits[7:0] (in big-endian mode) of the EMAC\_ADDR0\_LO register are written. For proper synchronization updates, the consecutive writes to this EMAC\_ADDR0\_LO register should be performed after at least four clock cycles in the destination clock domain.

Figure 30-90: EMAC\_ADDR[i]\_HI Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-145: EMAC\_ADDR[i]\_HI Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
|--------------------|------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31 (R/W)           | AE         | Address Enable. When the EMAC_ADDR[i]_HI.AE bit is set (=1), the address filter module uses the second MAC address for perfect filtering. When EMAC_ADDR[i]_HI.AE = 0, the address filter module ignores the address for filtering. 0 Address is Ignored                                                                          |
| 30 (R/W)           | SA         | 1 Address is Enabled Source Address. When the EMAC_ADDR[i]_HI.SA bit is set (=1), MAC address 1 [47:0] is used to compare with the SA fields of the received packet. When EMAC_ADDR[i]_HI.SA = 0, MAC address 1 [47:0] is used to compare with the DA fields of the received pack- et. 0 Compare with Destination Address Address |
| 30 (R/W)           |            | 1 Compare with Source                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| 30 (R/W)           |            |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

Table 30-145: EMAC\_ADDR[i]\_HI Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
|--------------------|------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 29:24 (R/W)        | MBC        | Mask Byte Control. These bits are mask control bits for comparing each of the MAC address bytes. When set (=1), the MAC does not compare the corresponding byte of received DA or SA with the contents of MAC address 1 registers. Each bit controls the masking of the bytes as follows: Bit 29: EMAC_ADDR[i]_HI [15:8] Bit 28: EMAC_ADDR[i]_HI [7:0] Bit 27: EMAC_ADDR[i]_HI [31:24] .. Bit 24: EMAC_ADDR[i]_HI [7:0] Filter a group of addresses (known as group address filtering) by masking one or more bytes of the address. |
| 23:16 (R/W)        | DCS        | DMAChannel Select. When EMAC_MAC_EXT_CFG.PDC = 0, the EMAC_ADDR[i]_HI.DCS field contains the binary representation of the DMAchannel number to which an Rx pack- et whose DA matches the MAC Address(n) content is routed. When EMAC_MAC_EXT_CFG.PDC = 1, the EMAC_ADDR[i]_HI.DCS field contains the one-hot representation of one or more DMAchannel numbers to which an Rx packet whose DA matches the MAC address(n) content is routed.                                                                                          |
| 15:0 (R/W)         | ADDRHI     | MAC Address1 [47:32]. The EMAC_ADDR[i]_HI.ADDRHI field contains the upper 16 bits[47:32] of the second 6-byte MAC address.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — Auxiliary Time Stamp Nanoseconds Register

<!-- source: 073_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2178–2178 -->

## Auxiliary Time Stamp Nanoseconds Register

The EMAC\_TM\_AUXTS\_NSEC register, along with EMAC\_TM\_AUXTS\_SEC register, gives the 64-bit time stamp stored as auxiliary snapshot. These two registers form the read port of a 64-bit wide FIFO with a depth of 4, 8, or 16 as selected while configuring the IP .

Multiple snapshots can be stored in this FIFO. Bits[29:25] in EMAC\_TM\_STAT register indicate the fill-level of the FIFO. The top of the FIFO is removed only when the last byte of EMAC\_TM\_AUXTS\_SEC register is read. In the Little Endian mode, this means when bits[31:24] are read and in Big Endian mode, bits[7:0] are read.

Figure 30-93: EMAC\_TM\_AUXTS\_NSEC Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-148: EMAC\_TM\_AUXTS\_NSEC Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                  |
|--------------------|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 30:0               | AUXTSLO    | Auxiliary Time Stamp. The EMAC_TM_AUXTS_NSEC.AUXTSLO field contains the lower 31 bits (nanosec- onds field) of the auxiliary time stamp. |
| (R/NW)             |            |                                                                                                                                          |

| 23 (R/W)           | GPSLCE     | Giant Packet Size Limit Control Enable. When the EMAC_MAC_CFG.GPSLCE bit is set, the MAC considers the value in EMAC_MAC_EXT_CFG.GPSL to declare a received packet as giant packet. When EMAC_MAC_CFG.GPSLCE = 0, the MAC considers a received packet as giant packet when its size is greater than 1,518 bytes (1522 bytes for tagged packet). The watchdog timeout limit, jumbo packet enable and 2K packet enable have higher precedence over the EMAC_MAC_CFG.GPSLCE bit, that is the MAC considers a re- ceived packet as giant packet when its size is greater than 9,018 bytes (9,022 bytes for tagged packet) with jumbo packet enabled and greater than 2,000 bytes with 2K pack- et enabled. The watchdog timeout, if enabled, terminates the received packet when watchdog limit is reached. The MAC issues a packet abort status, along with the excessive deferral er- ror bit set in the Tx packet status, when the Tx state machine is deferred for more than 24,288 bit times in 10 or 100 Mbps mode. If the MAC is configured for 1000 Mbps operation, the threshold for deferral is 155,680 bits times. Deferral begins when the transmitter is ready to transmit, but it is prevented because of an active carrier sense signal (CRS) on GMII or MII. The defer time is not cumulative. For example, if the transmitter defers for 10,000 bit times because the CRS signal is active and the CRS signal becomes inactive, the trans- mitter transmits and collision happens. Because of collision, the transmitter needs to back off and then defer again after back off completion. In such a scenario, the deferral timer is reset (=0), and it is restarted. When EMAC_MAC_CFG.DC = 0, the deferral check function is disabled and the MAC defers until the CRS signal goes inactive. ## MAC Split Mode and Offset Configuration Register

The EMAC\_SPLM\_OFST\_CFG register contains the split mode control field and offset field for the split header feature.

Figure 30-98: EMAC\_SPLM\_OFST\_CFG Register Diagram

|--------------------|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 24 (R/W)           | SAVE       | Split AV Enable. When EMAC_SPLM_OFST_CFG.SAVE = 1, and the received packet is an AV Type packet, the header is split at SAVO bytes from the beginning of Length/Type field of the packet, for L2 Split. When EMAC_SPLM_OFST_CFG.SAVE = 0, header is split at SPLOFST bytes from the beginning of Length/Type field of the frame, for L2 Split.                                     | Split AV Enable. When EMAC_SPLM_OFST_CFG.SAVE = 1, and the received packet is an AV Type packet, the header is split at SAVO bytes from the beginning of Length/Type field of the packet, for L2 Split. When EMAC_SPLM_OFST_CFG.SAVE = 0, header is split at SPLOFST bytes from the beginning of Length/Type field of the frame, for L2 Split.                                     |
| 22:16 (R/W)        | SAVO       | Split AV Offset. When SAVE bit is set (=1), and the received packet is an AV Type packet, the EMAC_SPLM_OFST_CFG.SAVO field indicates the value of the offset from the be- ginning of Length/Type field at which header should be split, when appropriate SPLM is selected. The reset value of this field is 2 bytes, indicating a split at L2 header. Value is in terms of bytes. | Split AV Offset. If the received packet size is greater than the value programmed in the EMAC_MAC_EXT_CFG.GPSL field in units of bytes, the MAC declares the received packet as giant packet. The value programmed in this field must be greater than or equal to 1,518 bytes. Any other programmed value is considered as 1,518 bytes. For VLAN tagged packets, the MAC adds 4 bytes to the programmed value. When the enable double VLAN processing option is selected, the MAC adds 8 bytes to the pro- grammed value for double VLAN tagged packets. The value in this field is applicable when EMAC_MAC_CFG.GPSLCE = 1. |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — Hash Table Register 0

<!-- source: 085_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2216–2216 -->

## Hash Table Register 0

The EMAC\_HASHTBL\_REG0 register contains the first 32 bits of the hash table.

The hash table is used for group address filtering. For hash filtering, the content of the destination address in the incoming packet is passed through the CRC logic and the upper six bits of 64-bit hash (eight in 256-bit hash) bits of the CRC register are used to index the content of the hash table. The most significant bits determines the register to be used (Hash Table Register n), and the least significant five bits determine the bit within the register. For example, a hash value of 6'b100000 (in 64-bit Hash) selects bit 0 of the Hash Table Register 1, a value of 8b'10111111 (in 256-bit hash) selects bit 31 of the Hash Table Register 5.

The hash value of the destination address is calculated in the following way:

1. Calculate the 32-bit CRC for the DA (See IEEE 802.3, Section 3.2.8 for the steps to calculate CRC32).
2. Perform bitwise reversal for the value obtained in Step 1.
3. Take the upper 6 (or 7 or 8) bits from the value obtained in step 2.

If the corresponding bit value of the register is 1'b1, the packet is accepted. Otherwise, it is rejected. If EMAC\_MACPKT\_FILT.PM = 1, all multicast packets are accepted regardless of the multicast hash values.

The hash table register is configured to be double-synchronized to the (G)MII clock domain; the synchronization is triggered only when bits[31:24] (in little-endian mode) or bits[7:0] (in big-endian mode) of the Hash Table Register n registers are written.

Hence, consecutive writes to this register should be performed only after at least four clock cycles in the (G)MII clock domain.

Figure 30-105: EMAC\_HASHTBL\_REG0 Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                               |
|--------------------|------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:0 (R/W)         | HT31T0     | MAC Hash Table First 32 Bits. The EMAC_HASHTBL_REG0.HT31T0 field contains the first 32 bits [31:0] of the hash table. |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — Hash Table Register 1

<!-- source: 086_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2217–2217 -->

## Hash Table Register 1

The EMAC\_HASHTBL\_REG1 register contains the second 32 bits of the hash table.

The hash table is used for group address filtering. For hash filtering, the content of the destination address in the incoming packet is passed through the CRC logic and the upper six bits of 64-bit hash (eight in 256-bit hash) bits of the CRC register are used to index the content of the hash table. The most significant bits determines the register to be used (Hash Table Register n), and the least significant five bits determine the bit within the register. For example, a hash value of 6'b100000 (in 64-bit Hash) selects bit 0 of the Hash Table Register 1, a value of 8b'10111111 (in 256-bit hash) selects bit 31 of the Hash Table Register 5.

The hash value of the destination address is calculated in the following way:

1. Calculate the 32-bit CRC for the DA (See IEEE 802.3, Section 3.2.8 for the steps to calculate CRC32).
2. Perform bitwise reversal for the value obtained in Step 1.
3. Take the upper 6 (or 7 or 8) bits from the value obtained in step 2.

If the corresponding bit value of the register is 1'b1, the packet is accepted. Otherwise, it is rejected. If EMAC\_MACPKT\_FILT.PM = 1, all multicast packets are accepted regardless of the multicast hash values. The hash table register is configured to be double-synchronized to the (G)MII clock domain; the synchronization is triggered only when bits[31:24] (in little-endian mode) or bits[7:0] (in big-endian mode) of the Hash Table Register n registers are written.

Hence, consecutive writes to this register should be performed only after at least four clock cycles in the (G)MII clock domain.

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — Indirect Access Control Register

<!-- source: 093_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2224–2225 -->

## Indirect Access Control Register

The EMAC\_INDR\_ACC\_CTL register provides the indirect access control and status for MAC\_&lt;MSEl&gt;\_&lt;AOFF&gt; registers.

Figure 30-113: EMAC\_INDR\_ACC\_CTL Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-168: EMAC\_INDR\_ACC\_CTL Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|--------------------|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 19:16 (R/W)        | MSEL       | Mode Select. The EMAC_INDR_ACC_CTL.MSEL field is used in indirect access of MAC_<MSEL>_<AOFF>. The EMAC_INDR_ACC_CTL.MSEL field must be set along with initiation of read/write to MAC_<MSEL>_<AOFF> and should not be changed until the OB is cleared. Values: - 0000:Typ_RXQ_ (Type based RXQ mapping) - 0001-1111: Reserved                                                                                                             |
| 15:8 (R/W)         | AOFF       | Address Offset. The EMAC_INDR_ACC_CTL.AOFF field is used in indirect access of MAC_<MSEL>_<AOFF>. The EMAC_INDR_ACC_CTL.AOFF field must be con- figured along with initiation of read/write to MAC_<MSEL>_<AOFF> and should not be changed until the OB is cleared. Values: - 00000000: IndReg0(Indirect register 0) - 00000001: IndReg1(Indirect register 1) - ... - 00000111: IndReg7(Indirect register 7) - 00001000-11111111: Reserved |

Table 30-168: EMAC\_INDR\_ACC\_CTL Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|--------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 5 (R/W)            | AUTO                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Auto Increment Enable. The EMAC_INDR_ACC_CTL.AUTO bit enables the address offset auto increment feature. When set (=1), AOFF is incremented by 1. Software should ensure not to cause a wrap condition. Byte wise read/write is not supported when auto increment is enabled. When the EMAC_INDR_ACC_CTL.AUTO bit is cleared (=0), AOFF is not incremented automatically. Software should program the correct Address Offset for each access.                                                                                                                                                                                |
| 1 (R/W)            | COM                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Command Type. The EMAC_INDR_ACC_CTL.COM bit indicates the register access type. - 1: Indi- cates a read operation. - 0: Indicates a write operation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| 1 (R/W)            | COM                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | 0 Write Operation                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| 0 (R/W)            | OB Operation Busy. The EMAC_INDR_ACC_CTL.OB bit is set along with a read or write command for initiating the indirect access to MAC_<MSEL>_<AOFF> register. The EMAC_INDR_ACC_CTL.OB bit is cleared (=0) when the read or write command to MAC_<MSEL>_<AOFF> register is complete. The next indirect register access can be initiated only after EMAC_INDR_ACC_CTL.OB = 0. During a write operation, the bit is cleared (=0) only after the data has been written into MAC_<MSEL>_<AOFF> register. During a read operation, the data should be read from the EMAC_INDR_ACC_DAT register only after EMAC_INDR_ACC_CTL.OB = 0. | OB Operation Busy. The EMAC_INDR_ACC_CTL.OB bit is set along with a read or write command for initiating the indirect access to MAC_<MSEL>_<AOFF> register. The EMAC_INDR_ACC_CTL.OB bit is cleared (=0) when the read or write command to MAC_<MSEL>_<AOFF> register is complete. The next indirect register access can be initiated only after EMAC_INDR_ACC_CTL.OB = 0. During a write operation, the bit is cleared (=0) only after the data has been written into MAC_<MSEL>_<AOFF> register. During a read operation, the data should be read from the EMAC_INDR_ACC_DAT register only after EMAC_INDR_ACC_CTL.OB = 0. |

## Inner VLAN Tag Inclusion or Replacement Register

The EMAC\_INVLAN\_INCL register contains the inner VLAN tag to be inserted or replaced in the transmit packet. It also contains the inner VLAN tag insertion controls.

Figure 30-115: EMAC\_INVLAN\_INCL Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-170: EMAC\_INVLAN\_INCL Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|--------------------|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 20 (R/W)           | VLTI       | VLAN Tag Input. When the EMAC_INVLAN_INCL.VLTI bit is set, it indicates that the VLAN tag to be inserted or replaced in Tx packet should be taken from the Tx descriptor.                                                                                                                      | VLAN Tag Input. When the EMAC_INVLAN_INCL.VLTI bit is set, it indicates that the VLAN tag to be inserted or replaced in Tx packet should be taken from the Tx descriptor.                                                                                                                      |
| 20 (R/W)           | VLTI       | 0                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | VLAN Tag Input is Disabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| 20 (R/W)           | VLTI       | 1                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | VLAN Tag Input is Enabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| 19 (R/W)           | CSVL       | C-VLAN or S-VLAN. When the EMAC_INVLAN_INCL.CSVL bit is set, S-VLAN type (0x88A8) is insert- ed or replaced in the 17th and 18th bytes of transmitted packets. When EMAC_INVLAN_INCL.CSVL = 0, C-VLAN type (0x8100) is inserted or replaced in the 17th and 18th bytes of transmitted packets. | C-VLAN or S-VLAN. When the EMAC_INVLAN_INCL.CSVL bit is set, S-VLAN type (0x88A8) is insert- ed or replaced in the 17th and 18th bytes of transmitted packets. When EMAC_INVLAN_INCL.CSVL = 0, C-VLAN type (0x8100) is inserted or replaced in the 17th and 18th bytes of transmitted packets. |
| 19 (R/W)           | CSVL       | 0                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | C-VLAN Type (0x8100) is Inserted                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| 19 (R/W)           | CSVL       | 1                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | S-VLAN Type (0x88A8) is Inserted                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| 18 (R/W)           | VLP        | VLAN Priority Control. When the EMAC_INVLAN_INCL.VLP bit is set, the VLC field is used for VLAN deletion, insertion, or replacement. When EMAC_INVLAN_INCL.VLP = 0, the TDES2.VTIR descriptor control is used and the VLC field is ignored.                                                    | VLAN Priority Control. When the EMAC_INVLAN_INCL.VLP bit is set, the VLC field is used for VLAN deletion, insertion, or replacement. When EMAC_INVLAN_INCL.VLP = 0, the TDES2.VTIR descriptor control is used and the VLC field is ignored.                                                    |
| 18 (R/W)           | VLP        | 0                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | VLAN Priority Control is Disabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| 18 (R/W)           | VLP        | 1                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | VLAN Priority Control is Enabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

Table 30-170: EMAC\_INVLAN\_INCL Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|--------------------|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 17:16 (R/W)        | VLC        | VLAN Tag Control in Transmit Packets. The EMAC_INVLAN_INCL.VLC field indicates the VLAN tag control in transmit packets. 2'b00: No VLAN tag deletion, insertion, or replacement 2'b01: VLAN tag deletion. The MAC removes the VLAN type (bytes 17 and 18) and VLAN tag (bytes 19 and 20) of all transmitted packets with VLAN tags. 2'b10: VLAN tag insertion. The MAC inserts VLT in bytes 19 and 20 of the packet after inserting the Type value (0x8100 or 0x88a8) in bytes 17 and 18. This operation is performed on all transmitted packets, irrespective of whether they already have a VLAN tag. 2'b11: VLAN tag replacement. The MAC replaces VLT in bytes 19 and 20 of all VLAN-type transmitted packets (Bytes 17 and 18 are 0x8100 or 0x88a8). Note: Changes to this field take effect only on the start of a packet. If this register field is written to when a packet is being transmitted, only the subsequent packet can use the updated value; the current packet does not use the updated value. 0 No VLAN Tag Deletion, Insertion, or Replacement |
| 15:0 (R/W)         | VLT        | VLAN Tag for Transmit Packets. The EMAC_INVLAN_INCL.VLT field contains the value of the VLAN tag to be in- serted or replaced. The value must only be changed when the transmit lines are inac- tive or during the initialization phase. Bits[15:13] are the User Priority field, Bit 12 is the CFI/DEI field, and bits[11:0] are the VID field in the VLAN tag. The following list describes the bits of this field: - Bits[15:13]: User Priority - Bit 12: Canonical Format Indicator (CFI) or Drop Eligible Indicator (DEI) - Bits[11:0]: VLAN Identifier (VID) field of VLAN tag                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

If the time stamp feature is enabled, the EMAC_MAC_ISTAT.TSIS bit is set when any of the following conditions are true: The system time value is equal to or exceeds the value specified in the Target Time High and Low registers. If the Auxiliary Snapshot feature is enabled, the EMAC_MAC_ISTAT.TSIS bit is set when the auxiliary snapshot trigger is asserted. The EMAC\_L3L4\_CTL[i] register controls the operations of filter 0 of layer 3 and layer 4.

When EMAC_L3L4_CTL[i].DMCHEN = 0, the DMAchannel is not decided by this filter. 0 DMAChannel Select is Disabled |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — LPI Control and Status Register

<!-- source: 100_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2246–2249 -->

## LPI Control and Status Register

The EMAC\_LPI\_CTLSTAT register controls the LPI functions and provides the LPI interrupt status. The status bits are cleared when this register is read.

Figure 30-120: EMAC\_LPI\_CTLSTAT Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-175: EMAC\_LPI\_CTLSTAT Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
|--------------------|------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 20 (R/W)           | LPIATE     | LPI Timer Enable. The EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.LPIATE bit controls the automatic entry of the MAC transmitter into and exit out of the LPI state. When LPIATE, LPITXA and LPIEN bits are set, the MAC transmitter enters LPI state only when the complete MAC TX data path is IDLE for a period indicated by the EMAC_LPI_ENTR_TMR register. After entering LPI state, if the data path becomes non-IDLE (due to a new packet be- ing accepted for transmission), the transmitter exits LPI state but does not clear LPIEN bit. This enables the re-entry into LPI state when it is IDLE again. When EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.LPIATE = 0, the LPI auto timer is disabled and MAC transmitter enters LPI state based on the settings of LPITXA and LPIEN bit de- scriptions. |
| 20 (R/W)           | LPIATE     | 0 LPI Timer is Disabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| 20 (R/W)           | LPIATE     | 1 LPI Timer is Enabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

Table 30-175: EMAC\_LPI\_CTLSTAT Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
|--------------------|------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 19 (R/W)           | LPITXA     | LPI Tx Automate. The EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.LPITXA bit controls the behavior of the MAC when it is entering or coming out of the LPI mode on the transmit side. If the EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.LPITXA and LPIEN bits are set (=1), the MAC en- ters the LPI mode only after all outstanding packets (in the IP) and pending packets (in the application interface) have been transmitted. The MAC comes out of the LPI mode when the application sends any packet for transmission or the application issues a Tx FIFO Flush command. In addition, the MAC automatically clears the LPIEN bit when it exits the LPI state. If Tx FIFO flush is set in EMAC_TQ0_OPMODE.FTQ, when the MAC is in the LPI mode, it exits the LPI mode. When the EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.LPITXA bit is 0, the LPIEN bit directly controls behavior of the MAC when it is entering or coming out of the LPI mode. 0 LPI Tx Automate is Disabled |
| 18 (R/W)           | PLSEN      | PHY Link Status Enable. The EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.PLSEN bit enables the link status received on the RGMII receive paths to be used for activating the LPI LS TIMER. When the EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.PLSEN bit is set, the MAC uses the link-status bits of the EMAC_PHYIF_CTLSTAT register and the PLS bit for the LPI LS timer trigger. When EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.PLSEN = 0, the MAC ignores the link-status bits of the EMAC_PHYIF_CTLSTAT register and takes only the PLS bit.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| 17 (R/W)           | PLS        | 1 PHY Link Status is Enabled PHY Link Status. The EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.PLS bit indicates the link status of the PHY. The MAC transmitter asserts the LPI pattern only when the link status is up (OKAY) at least for the time indicated by the LPI LS TIMER. When the EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.PLS bit is set, the link is considered to be okay (UP) and when EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.PLS = 0, the link is considered to be down. 0 Link is Down 1 Link is Okay (UP)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

Table 30-175: EMAC\_LPI\_CTLSTAT Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|--------------------|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 16 (R/W)           | LPIEN      | LPI Enable. When the EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.LPIEN bit is set, it instructs the MAC transmit- ter to enter the LPI state. When EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.LPIEN = 0, it instructs the MAC to exit the LPI state and resume normal transmission. The EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.LPIEN bit is cleared when the LPITXA bit is set and the MAC exits the LPI state because of the arrival of a new packet for transmission.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| 9 (R/NW)           | RLPIST     | Receive LPI State. When the EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.RLPIST bit is set, it indicates that the MAC is receiving the LPI pattern on the GMII or MII interface.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| 8 (R/NW)           | TLPIST     | Transmit LPI State. When the EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.TLPIST bit is set, it indicates that the MAC is transmitting the LPI pattern on the GMII or MII interface.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| 3 (R/NW)           | RLPIEX     | Receive LPI Exit. The EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.RLPIEX bit is cleared by a read into this register (or the EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.RLPIEX bit is written to 1 when EMAC_CSR_SW_CTL.RCWE = 1). Note: The EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.RLPIEX bit might not be set if the MAC stops receiving the LPI pattern for a very short duration, such as, less than three clock cycles of SCLK0. 0 Receive LPI Exit Not Detected 1 Receive LPI Exit Detected |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — Transmit LPI Entry Timer Register

<!-- source: 101_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2250–2250 -->

## Transmit LPI Entry Timer Register

The EMAC\_LPI\_ENTR\_TMR register controls the Tx LPI entry timer. This counter is enabled only when EMAC\_LPI\_CTLSTAT.LPITE = 1.

Figure 30-121: EMAC\_LPI\_ENTR\_TMR Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-176: EMAC\_LPI\_ENTR\_TMR Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|--------------------|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 19:3 (R/W)         | LPIET      | LPI Entry Timer. The EMAC_LPI_ENTR_TMR.LPIET field specifies the time in microseconds the MAC waits to enter LPI mode, after it has transmitted all the frames. The EMAC_LPI_ENTR_TMR.LPIET field is valid and used only when LPITE and LPITXA are set (=1). Bits [2:0] are read-only so that the granularity of this timer is in steps of 8 microsec- onds. |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — LPI Timers Control Register

<!-- source: 102_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2251–2251 -->

## LPI Timers Control Register

The EMAC\_LPI\_TMRSCTL register controls the timeout values in the LPI states. It specifies the time for which the MAC transmits the LPI pattern and also the time for which the MAC waits before resuming the normal transmission.

Figure 30-122: EMAC\_LPI\_TMRSCTL Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-177: EMAC\_LPI\_TMRSCTL Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|--------------------|------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 25:16 (R/W)        | LST        | LPI LS Timer. The EMAC_LPI_TMRSCTL.LST field specifies the minimum time (in milliseconds) for which the link status from the PHY should be up (OKAY) before the LPI pattern can be transmitted to the PHY. The MAC does not transmit the LPI pattern even when the LPIEN bit is set unless the LPI LS Timer reaches the programmed terminal count. The default value of the LPI LS Timer is 1000 (1 sec) as defined in the IEEE standard. |
| 15:0 (R/W)         | TWT        | LPI TWTimer. The EMAC_LPI_TMRSCTL.TWT field specifies the minimum time (in microsec- onds) for which the MAC waits after it stops transmitting the LPI pattern to the PHY and before it resumes the normal transmission. The TLPIEX status bit is set after the expiry of this timer.                                                                                                                                                     |
