# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — Layer 3 Address 0 Register 7

<!-- source: 103_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2252–2252 -->

## Layer 3 Address 0 Register 7

For IPv4 packets, the EMAC\_L3\_ADDR0\_REG7 register contains the 32-bit IP Source Address field. For IPv6 packets, it contains bits[31:0] of the 128-bit IP Source Address or Destination Address field.

Figure 30-123: EMAC\_L3\_ADDR0\_REG7 Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-178: EMAC\_L3\_ADDR0\_REG7 Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|--------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:0 (R/W)         | L3A        | Layer 3 Address 0 Field. When EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L3PEN and EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L3SAM = 1, the EMAC_L3_ADDR0_REG7.L3A field contains the value to be matched with bits[31:0] of the IP Source Address field in the IPv6 packets. When EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L3PEN and EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L3DAM = 1, the EMAC_L3_ADDR0_REG7.L3A field contains the value to be matched with bits[31:0] of the IP Destination Address field in the IPv6 packets. When EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L3PEN = 0 and EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L3SAM = 1, the EMAC_L3_ADDR0_REG7.L3A field contains the value to be matched with the IP Source Address field in the IPv4 packets. |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — Layer 4 Address Register [i]

<!-- source: 111_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2260–2260 -->

## Layer 4 Address Register [i]

The EMAC\_L4\_ADDR7 register is double synchronized to the Rx clock domain. Thus, for proper synchronization updates, the program should perform consecutive writes to the same layer 3/4 address registers only after at least four clock cycles delay of the (G) MII clock domain.

Figure 30-131: EMAC\_L4\_ADDR7 Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-186: EMAC\_L4\_ADDR7 Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
|--------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:16 (R/W)        | L4DP       | Layer 4 Destination Port Number Field. When EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L4PEN = 0 and EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L4DPM =1, this field contains the value to be matched with the TCP Destination Port Number field in the IPv4 or IPv6 packets. When the EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L4PEN = 0 and EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L4DPM =1, this field contains the value to be matched with the UDP Destination Port Num- ber field in the IPv4 or IPv6 packets.                    |
| 15:0 (R/W)         | L4SP       | Layer 4 Source Port Number Field. When EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L4PEN = 0 and EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L4SPM =1, the EMAC_L4_ADDR7.L4SP field contains the value to be matched with the TCP Source Port Number field in the IPv4 or IPv6 packets. When the EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L4PEN = 1 and EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L4SPM =1, the EMAC_L4_ADDR7.L4SP field contains the value to be matched with the UDP Source Port Number field in the IPv4 or IPv6 packets. |

The EMAC\_LOG\_MSG\_INTVL register contains the periodic intervals for automatic PTP packet generation.

This is used to schedule the periodic Pdelay request packet transmission. Allowed values are -15 to 15.Negative value must be represented in 2's-complement form. For example, if the required value is -1, the value programmed must be 0xFF.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Log Min Pdelay_Req Interval. The EMAC_LOG_MSG_INTVL.LMPDRI field indicates logMinPdelayReqInterval of PTP node. This is used to schedule the periodic Pdelay request packet transmission. Allowed values are -15 to 15.Negative value must be represented in 2's-complement form. For example, if the required value is -1, the value programmed must be 0xFF.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

The EMAC module receiver processes this value from the received DelayResp messages and updates this field accordingly. In completer mode, the host must not write/update this register unless it has to override the received value. In requester mode, the sum of this field and logSyncInterval (LSI) field is provided in the logMinDelayReqInterval field of the generated multicast Delay_Resp PTP mes- sage. Access restriction applies. Updated based on the event. Write 1 to set. Write 0 to clear. | Delay_Req to SYNC Ratio. The EMAC module receiver processes this value from the received DelayResp messages and updates this field accordingly. In completer mode, the host must not write/update this register unless it has to override the received value. In requester mode, the sum of this field and logSyncInterval (LSI) field is provided in the logMinDelayReqInterval field of the generated multicast Delay_Resp PTP mes- sage. Access restriction applies. Updated based on the event. Write 1 to set. Write 0 to clear. |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — MDIO Address Register

<!-- source: 114_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2264–2268 -->

## MDIO Address Register

The EMAC\_MDIO\_ADDR register controls the management cycles to external PHY through a management interface.

Figure 30-134: EMAC\_MDIO\_ADDR Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-189: EMAC\_MDIO\_ADDR Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|--------------------|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 27 (R/W)           | PSE        | Preamble Suppression Enable. When the EMAC_MDIO_ADDR.PSE bit is set, the SMA suppresses the 32-bit pream- ble and transmits MDIO frames with only 1 preamble bit. When the EMAC_MDIO_ADDR.PSE bit is 0, the MDIO frame always has 32 bits of preamble as defined in the IEEE specifications. |
| 27 (R/W)           | PSE        | 0 Preamble Suppression Disabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| 27 (R/W)           | PSE        | 1 Preamble Suppression Enabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

Table 30-189: EMAC\_MDIO\_ADDR Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|--------------------|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 26 (R/W)           | BTB        | Back to Back Transactions. When the EMAC_MDIO_ADDR.BTB bit is set and the NTC has value greater than 0, the MAC informs the completion of a read or write command at the end of frame transfer (before the trailing clocks are transmitted). The software can thus initiate the next command which is executed immediately irrespective of the number trailing clocks generated for the previous frame. When EMAC_MDIO_ADDR.BTB = 0, then the read/write command completion (GB is cleared) only after the trailing clocks are generated. In this mode, it is ensured that the NTC is always generated after each frame. The EMAC_MDIO_ADDR.BTB bit must not be set when NTC=0. 0 Back to Back Transactions Disabled |
| 25:21 (R/W)        | PA         | Physical Layer Address. The EMAC_MDIO_ADDR.PA field indicates which Clause 22 PHY devices (out of 32 devices) the MAC is accessing. The EMAC_MDIO_ADDR.PA field indicates which Clause 45 capable PHYs (out of 32 PHYs) the MAC is accessing.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| 20:16 (R/W)        | RDA        | Register/Device Address. The EMAC_MDIO_ADDR.RDA field selects the PHY register in selected Clause 22 PHY device. These bits select the Device (MMD) in selected Clause 45 capable PHY.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| 14:12 (R/W)        | NTC        | Number of Trailing Clocks. The EMAC_MDIO_ADDR.NTC field controls the number of trailing clock cycles gen- erated on ETHx_MDC (MDC) after the end of transmission of MDIO frame. The valid values can be from 0 to 7. Programming the value to 3'h3 indicates that there are additional three clock cycles on the MDCline after the end of MDIO frame transfer.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

|--------------------|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

The EMAC_MDIO_ADDR.CR field indicates the frequency of the MDCclock accord- ing to the SCLK0 frequency used: 0000: SCLK0 = 60-100 MHz; MDCclock = SCLK0/42 0001: SCLK0 = 100-150 MHz; MDCclock = SCLK0/62 0010: SCLK0 = 20-35 MHz; MDCclock = SCLK0/16 0011: SCLK0 = 35-60 MHz; MDCclock = SCLK0/26 | SCLK0 Range. The EMAC_MDIO_ADDR.CR field indicates the frequency of the MDCclock accord- ing to the SCLK0 frequency used: 0000: SCLK0 = 60-100 MHz; MDCclock = SCLK0/42 0001: SCLK0 = 100-150 MHz; MDCclock = SCLK0/62 0010: SCLK0 = 20-35 MHz; MDCclock = SCLK0/16 0011: SCLK0 = 35-60 MHz; MDCclock = SCLK0/26 |

| 4                  | SKAP       | 0                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Skip Address Packet is Disabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| 4                  | SKAP       | 1                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Skip Address Packet is Enabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

|--------------------|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

The EMAC_MDIO_ADDR.GOC_1 bit is higher bit of the operation command to the PHY, GOC_1 and GOC_O is encoded as follows: 00: Reserved 01: Write 10: Post read increment address for clause 45 PHY 11: Read When clause 22 PHY is enabled, only write and read commands are valid. 0 GMII Operation Command 1 is Disabled | GMII Operation Command 1. EMAC_MDIO_ADDR.GOC_0 is the lower bit of the operation command to the PHY. When in SMA mode (MDIO requester) the EMAC_MDIO_ADDR.GOC_0 bit along with GOC_1 determines the operation to be performed to the PHY.                                                                                                        |
| 2 (R/W)            | GOC_0      | 0                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | GMII Operation Command 0 is Disabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

When EMAC_MDIO_ADDR.C45E = 0, Clause 22 capable PHY is con- nected to MDIO.                                                                                                                                                           | Clause 45 PHY Enable. When the EMAC_MDIO_ADDR.C45E bit is set, Clause 45 capable PHY is connected to MDIO. When EMAC_MDIO_ADDR.C45E = 0, Clause 22 capable PHY is con- nected to MDIO.                                                                                                                                                           |
| 1 (R/W)            | C45E       | 0                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Clause 45 PHY is Disabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| 1 (R/W)            | C45E       | 1                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Clause 45 PHY is Enabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

Table 30-189: EMAC\_MDIO\_ADDR Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
|--------------------|------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 0 (R/W)            | GB         | GMII Busy. The application sets the EMAC_MDIO_ADDR.GB bit to instruct the SMA to initiate a read or write access to the MDIO completer. The MAC clears the EMAC_MDIO_ADDR.GB bit after the MDIO frame transfer is completed. Hence the software must not write or change any of the fields in EMAC_MDIO_ADDR and EMAC_MDIO_DATA registers as long as this bit is set. For write transfers, the application must first write 16-bit data in the GDl field (and also RA field when EMAC_MDIO_ADDR.C45E = 1) in EMAC_MDIO_DATA reg- ister before setting the EMAC_MDIO_ADDR.GB bit. When EMAC_MDIO_ADDR.C45E = 1, it should also write to EMAC_MDIO_DATA.RA before initiating a read transfer. When a read transfer is completed (GB=0), the data read from the PHY register is valid in EMAC_MDIO_DATA.GD. Note: Even if the addressed PHY is not present, there is no change in the functionality of the EMAC_MDIO_ADDR.GB bit. Access restriction applies. Write 1 to set. Self-cleared. Writing 0 has no effect. |
| 0 (R/W)            |            | 0 GMII Busy is Disabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| 0 (R/W)            |            | 1 GMII Busy is Enabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — MDIO Data Register

<!-- source: 115_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2269–2269 -->

## MDIO Data Register

The EMAC\_MDIO\_DATA register stores the write data to be written to the PHY register located at the address specified in EMAC\_MDIO\_ADDR. The EMAC\_MDIO\_DATA register also stores the read data from the PHY register located at the address specified by MDIO Address register.

Figure 30-135: EMAC\_MDIO\_DATA Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-190: EMAC\_MDIO\_DATA Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|--------------------|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:16 (R/W)        | RA         | Register Address. The EMAC_MDIO_DATA.RA field is valid only when EMAC_MDIO_ADDR.C45E = 1. It contains the register address in the PHY for the intended MDIO frame.                                               |
| 15:0 (R/W)         | GD         | GMII Data. The EMAC_MDIO_DATA.GD field contains the 16-bit data value read from the PHY after a management read operation or the 16-bit data value to be written to the PHY before a management write operation. |

| 18:17 (R/NW)       | LNKSPEED   | Link Speed. The EMAC_PHYIF_CTLSTAT.LNKSPEED bit indicates the current speed of the link.                               |
| 16 (R/NW)          | LNKMOD     | Link Mode. The EMAC_PHYIF_CTLSTAT.LNKMOD bit indicates the current mode of opera- tion of the link. 0 Half-duplex Mode |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — PPS n Interval Register

<!-- source: 117_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2272–2272 -->

## PPS n Interval Register

The EMAC\_PPS[n]\_INTVL register contains the number of units of sub-second increment value between the rising edges of ETH0\_PTPPPSn signal output.

Figure 30-137: EMAC\_PPS[n]\_INTVL Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-192: EMAC\_PPS[n]\_INTVL Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|--------------------|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:0 (R/W)         | PPSINT     | PPS Output Signal Interval. The EMAC_PPS[n]_INTVL.PPSINT field stores the interval between the rising edges of the ETH0_PTPPPSn signal output. The interval is stored in terms of number of units of sub-second increment value. Program one value less than the required interval. For example, if the PTP reference clock is 50 MHz (period of 20 ns), and desired interval between the rising edges of the ETH0_PTPPPSn signal output is 100 ns (that is, 5 units of sub-second increment val- ue), program value 4 (5-1) in this register. |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — PPS n Target Time Seconds Register

<!-- source: 119_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2274–2274 -->

## PPS n Target Time Seconds Register

The EMAC\_PPS[n]\_TGTM\_SEC register, along with the EMAC\_PPS[n]\_TGTM\_NSEC register, is used to schedule an interrupt event (bit 1 of EMAC\_TM\_STAT) when the system time exceeds the value programmed in these registers.

Figure 30-139: EMAC\_PPS[n]\_TGTM\_SEC Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-194: EMAC\_PPS[n]\_TGTM\_SEC Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
|--------------------|------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:0 (R/W)         | TSTRH      | PPS Target Time Seconds Register. The EMAC_PPS[n]_TGTM_SEC.TSTRH field stores the time in seconds. When the time stamp value matches or exceeds both target time stamp registers, the MAC starts or stops the PPS signal output and generates an interrupt (if enabled) based on the target time mode selected for the corresponding PPS output in the EMAC_PPS_CTL register. If EMAC_TM_CTL.PTGE = 1 with the presentation time control set in recovery mode, then these bits indicate the TPT being programmed by the application and in generation mode it indicates the CPT generated at the sampled trigger. |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — PPS n Width Register

<!-- source: 120_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2275–2275 -->

## PPS n Width Register

The EMAC\_PPS[n]\_WID register contains the number of units of sub-second increment value between the rising and corresponding falling edges of ETH0\_PTPPPSn signal output.

Figure 30-140: EMAC\_PPS[n]\_WID Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-195: EMAC\_PPS[n]\_WID Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|--------------------|------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:0 (R/W)         | PPSWIDTH   | PPS Output Signal Width. The EMAC_PPS[n]_WID.PPSWIDTH field store the width between the rising edge and corresponding falling edge of PPS signal output. The width is stored in terms of number of units of sub-second increment value. Program one value less than the required interval. For example, if PTP reference clock is 50 MHz (period of 20 ns), and width between the rising and corresponding falling edges of PPS signal output is 80 ns (that is, four units of sub-second increment value), program value 3 (4-1) in this register. Note: The value programmed in this register must be lesser than the value program- med in the EMAC_PPS[n]_INTVL register. |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — PPS Control Register

<!-- source: 121_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2276–2281 -->

## PPS Control Register

Bits[30:24] of the EMAC\_PPS\_CTL register are valid only when four flexible PPS outputs are selected. Bits[22:16] are valid only when three or more flexible PPS outputs are selected. Bits[14:8] are valid only when two or more flexible PPS outputs are selected. Bits[6:4] are valid only when flexible PPS feature is selected.

|--------------------|------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

| 31 (R/W)           | MCGREN3    | 0 PPS Mode                                                                                                            |
| 31 (R/W)           | MCGREN3    | 1 MCGR Mode                                                                                                           |

|--------------------|-------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

The EMAC_PPS_CTL.TRGTMODSEL3 field indicates the target time registers (EMAC_PPS[3]_TGTM_SEC and EMAC_PPS[3]_TGTM_NSEC) mode for PPS3 output signal.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| 30:29 (R/W)        | TRGTMODSEL3 | 0 Generate the Interrupt Only. Target time registers are programmed only for generating the interrupt event. | 3:0 (R/W)          | PPSCTRL_PPSCMD | PPS Output Frequency Control. The EMAC_PPS_CTL.PPSCTRL_PPSCMD field controls the frequency of the ETH0_PTPPPS0 output (PTP clock) signal. The default value is 0000, and the PPS output is 1 pulse (of width PTP clock) every second. For other values of EMAC_PPS_CTL.PPSCTRL_PPSCMD , the PPS output becomes a generated clock of following frequencies: - 0001: The binary rollover is 2 Hz, and the digital rollover is 1 Hz. - 0010: The binary rollover is 4 Hz, and the digital rollover is 2 Hz. - 0011: The binary rollover is 8 Hz; digital rollover is 4 Hz. - 0100: The binary rollover is 16 Hz; digital rollover is 8 Hz. ... - 1111: The binary rollover is 32.768 KHz; digital rollover is 16.384 KHz. See the Fixed Pulse-Per-Second Output topic for details. When EMAC_PPS_CTL.PPSCTRL_PPSCMD = 0011, the PPS (4 Hz) is a sequence of: Three clocks of 50 percent duty cycle and 268 ms period. A fourth clock of 195 ms period (134 ms low and 61 ms high). This behavior is due to the non-linear toggling of bits in the digital rollover mode in the EMAC_TM_NSEC register. For Flexible PPS Output (ETH0_PTPPPS0) control, programming the EMAC_PPS_CTL.PPSCTRL_PPSCMD bits with a non-zero value instructs the MAC to initiate an event. When the command is transferred or synchronized to the PTP clock domain, the bits are cleared automatically. Software should ensure that these bits are programmed only when they are 'all-zero'. When EMAC_PPS_CTL.MCGREN0 = 1, the EMAC_PPS_CTL.PPSCTRL_PPSCMD bits are treated as presentation time control bits: - 0000: MCGR operation is not carried out. If configured to this value in the middle of clock recovery or generation, all processing inputs are flushed. - 0001: Capture the presentation time at the rising edge of the EMAC0_MCG_PST trigger request into the EMAC_PPS[0]_TGTM_SEC register. - 0010: Capture the presentation time at the falling edge of the EMAC0_MCG_PST trigger request into the EMAC_PPS[0]_TGTM_SEC register. - 0011: Capture the presentation time at both edges of the EMAC0_MCG_PST trig- ger request into the EMAC_PPS[0]_TGTM_SEC register. - 0100-1000: Reserved - 1001: Toggle output on compare - 1010: Pulse output low on compare for one PTP clock cycle. - 1011: Pulse output high on compare for one PTP clock cycle. - 1100-1111: Reserved |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — MAC Packet Filter Register

## MAC Packet Filter Register

The EMAC\_MACPKT\_FILT register contains the filter controls for receiving packets. Some of the controls from this register go to the address check block of the MAC which performs the first level of address filtering. The second level of filtering is performed on the incoming packet based on other controls such as Pass Bad Packets and Pass Control Packets.

Figure 30-143: EMAC\_MACPKT\_FILT Register Diagram

|--------------------|------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31 (R/W)           | RA         | Receive All. When the EMAC_MACPKT_FILT.RA bit is set, the MAC receiver module passes all received packets to the application, irrespective of whether they pass the address filter or not. The result of the SA or DA filtering is updated (pass or fail) in the correspond- ing bit in the Rx status word. When EMAC_MACPKT_FILT.RA = 0, the receiver module passes only those packets to the application that pass the SA or DA address filter. 0 Receive All is Disabled Enabled |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — Presentation Time Update Register

<!-- source: 124_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2290–2290 -->

## Presentation Time Update Register

The EMAC\_PRSNTM\_UPDT register holds the 32-bit value of MAC 1722 Presentation Time in ns, that should be added to the Current Presentation Time Counter value. Init happens when EMAC\_TM\_CTL.TSINIT = 1, and update happens when EMAC\_TM\_CTL.TSUPDT = 1.

The EMAC\_PRSNTM\_UPDT register exists when DWC\_EQOS\_FLEXI\_PPS\_OUT\_EN is configured.

Figure 30-144: EMAC\_PRSNTM\_UPDT Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-199: EMAC\_PRSNTM\_UPDT Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
|--------------------|------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:0 (R/W)         | MPTU       | 1722 Presentation Time Update. The EMAC_PRSNTM_UPDT.MPTU field holds the init value or the update value for the presentation time. When used for update, this field holds the 32-bit value in ns, that should be added to the Current Presentation Time Counter value. When EMAC_TM_NSECUPDT.ADDSUB = 1, this value is directly used for subtraction. |

The EMAC\_PRSNTM\_NSEC register contains the 32-bit binary rollover equivalent time of the PTP system time in ns.

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — Queue 0 Transmit Flow Control Register

<!-- source: 126_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2292–2294 -->

## Queue 0 Transmit Flow Control Register

The EMAC\_Q0\_TXFLOW\_CTL register controls the generation and reception of the Control (Pause Command) packets by the flow control module of the MAC. A write to a register with the Busy bit set (=1) triggers the Flow Control block to generate a Pause packet. The fields of the control packet are selected as specified in the 802.3x specification, and the Pause Time value from this register is used in the Pause Time field of the control packet. The Busy bit remains set until the control packet is transferred onto the cable. The application must make sure that the Busy bit is cleared before writing to the register.

When the PFCE bit in the MAC\_Rx\_Flow\_Ctrl register is enabled, this register controls the generation of Priority Flow Control (PFC) frames with priorities mapped according to PSRQ0 in the MAC\_RxQ\_Ctrl2 register.

Figure 30-146: EMAC\_Q0\_TXFLOW\_CTL Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|--------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:16 (R/W)        | PT         | Pause Time. The EMAC_Q0_TXFLOW_CTL.PT field holds the value to be used in the Pause Time field in the Tx control packet. If the Pause Time bits are configured to be dou- ble-synchronized to the (G)MII clock domain, consecutive writes to this register should be performed only after at least four clock cycles in the destination clock do- main. |

The EMAC_Q0_TXFLOW_CTL.FCB_BPA bit initiates a Pause packet in the full-du- plex mode and activates the backpressure function in the half-duplex mode if the TFE bit is set. In full-duplex mode, the EMAC_Q0_TXFLOW_CTL.FCB_BPA bit should be read as 1'b0 before writing to this register. To initiate a Pause packet, the application must set the EMAC_Q0_TXFLOW_CTL.FCB_BPA bit to 1'b1. During Control packet trans- fer, the EMAC_Q0_TXFLOW_CTL.FCB_BPA bit continues to be set to indicate that a packet transmission is in progress. # Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — Queue [i] Transmit Flow Control Register

<!-- source: 127_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2295–2297 -->

## Queue [i] Transmit Flow Control Register

The EMAC\_Q[i]\_TXFLOW\_CTL register controls the generation and reception of the Control (Pause Command) packets by the Flow control module of the MAC. A write to a register with the Busy bit set (= 1) triggers the Flow Control block to generate a Pause packet. The fields of the control packet are selected as specified in the 802.3x specification, and the Pause Time value from this register is used in the Pause Time field of the control packet. The Busy bit remains set until the control packet is transferred onto the cable. The application must make sure that the Busy bit is cleared before writing to the register. (EMAC\_RXFLOW\_CTL.PFCE = 1.)

The register controls the generation of PFC control packets of priorities mapped per the PSRQn field in the EMAC\_RXQ\_CTL2.EMAC\_RXQ\_CTL3 registers.

Hence, consecutive writes to this register should be per- formed only after at least four clock cycles in the (G)MII clock domain. |

## Receive Queue Control 0 Register

The EMAC\_RXQ\_CTL0 register controls the queue management in the MAC receiver.

Note: In multiple Rx queues configuration, all the queues are disabled by default. Enable the Rx queue by programming the corresponding field in this register.

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — Receive Queue Control 1 Register

<!-- source: 129_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2301–2304 -->

## Receive Queue Control 1 Register

The EMAC\_RXQ\_CTL1 register controls the routing of multicast, broadcast, AV, DCB, and untagged packets to the Rx queues.

<!-- image -->

Queuing Control.

Figure 30-149: EMAC\_RXQ\_CTL1 Register Diagram

Table 30-204: EMAC\_RXQ\_CTL1 Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|--------------------|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 29 (R/W)           | TBRQE      | Type Field Based Rx Queuing Enable. When the EMAC_RXQ_CTL1.TBRQE bit is set, it enables the Type field based Rx queuing where the Type field of received packet is compared with programmed TYP field in MAC_TMRQ_Regs(n) and if a match occurs the packet is routed to the corre- sponding TMRQ field.                                                  |
| 28 (R/W)           | OMCBCQ     | Over-riding MC-BC Queue Priority Select. When set (=1), the EMAC_RXQ_CTL1.OMCBCQ bit indicates that the priority of MCBCQ is reduced and the received packet is first routed to PTPQ, AVCPQ, DCBCPQ depending on packet type. When cleared (=0), the EMAC_RXQ_CTL1.OMCBCQ bit indicates that the received multicast/broadcast packet is routed to MCBCQ. |
| 28 (R/W)           | OMCBCQ     | 0 Overriding MCBCQ Priority Disabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| 28 (R/W)           | OMCBCQ     | 1 Overriding MCBCQ Priority Enabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — Receive Queue Control 2 Register

<!-- source: 130_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2305–2306 -->

## Receive Queue Control 2 Register

The EMAC\_RXQ\_CTL2 register controls the routing of tagged packets based on the USP (user priority) field of the received packets to the Rx queues 0 to 3.

Figure 30-150: EMAC\_RXQ\_CTL2 Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-205: EMAC\_RXQ\_CTL2 Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
|--------------------|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:24 (R/W)        | PSRQ3      | Priorities Selected in the Receive Queue 3. The EMAC_RXQ_CTL2.PSRQ3 field selects the priorities assigned to Rx queue 3. All packets with priorities that match the values set in this field are routed to Rx queue 3. For example, if PSRQ3[6, 3] are set, packets with USP field equal to 3 or 6 are routed to Rx queue 3. The software must ensure that the content of this field is mutually ex- clusive to the PSRQ fields for other queues, that is, the same priority is not mapped to multiple Rx queues. This field also determines the priorities to be included in the PFC packet sent to re- mote station when Rx queue 3 crosses the flow control threshold settings. |
| 23:16 (R/W)        | PSRQ2      | Priorities Selected in the Receive Queue 2. The EMAC_RXQ_CTL2.PSRQ2 field selects the priorities assigned to Rx queue 2. All packets with priorities that match the values set in this field are routed to Rx queue 2. For example, if PSRQ2[1, 0] are set, packets with USP field equal to 1 or 0 are routed to Rx queue 2. The software must ensure that the content of this field is mutually ex- clusive to the PSRQ fields for other queues, that is, the same priority is not mapped to multiple Rx queues. This field also determines the priorities to be included in the PFC packet sent to re- mote station when Rx queue 2 crosses the flow control threshold settings. |

All packets with priorities that match the values set in this field are routed to Rx queue 1. For example, if PSRQ1[4] is set, packets with USP field equal to 4 are routed to Rx queue 1. The software must ensure that the content of this field is mutually exclusive to the PSRQ fields for other queues, that is, the same priority is not mapped to multi- ple Rx queues. This field also determines the priorities to be included in the PFC packet sent to re- mote station when Rx queue 1 crosses the flow control threshold settings.        |
| 7:0 (R/W)          | PSRQ0      | Priorities Selected in the Receive Queue 0. The EMAC_RXQ_CTL2.PSRQ0 field selects the priorities assigned to Rx queue 0. All packets with priorities that match the values configured in this field are routed to Rx queue 0. For example, if PSRQ0[5] is set, packets with USP field equal to 5 are routed to Rx queue 0. The software must ensure that the content of this field is mutually exclusive to the PSRQ fields for other queues, that is, the same priority is not mapped to multi- ple Rx queues. This field also determines the priorities to be included in the PFC packet sent to re- mote station when Rx queue 0 crosses the flow control threshold settings. |

## Receive Queue Control 3 Register

The EMAC\_RXQ\_CTL3 register controls the routing of tagged packets based on the USP (user priority) field of the received packets to the Rx queues 4 to 7.

Figure 30-151: EMAC\_RXQ\_CTL3 Register Diagram

All packets with priorities that match the values set in this field are routed to Rx queue 7. For example, if PSRQ7[7, 4] are set, packets with USP field equal to 7 or 4 are routed to Rx queue 7. The software must ensure that the content of this field is mutually ex- clusive to the PSRQ fields for other queues, that is, the same priority is not mapped to multiple Rx queues. This field also determines the priorities to be included in the PFC packet sent to re- mote station when Rx queue 7 crosses the flow control threshold settings. |
| 23:16 (R/W)        | PSRQ6      | Priorities Selected in the Receive Queue 6. The EMAC_RXQ_CTL3.PSRQ6 field selects the priorities assigned to Rx queue 6. All packets with priorities that match the values set in this field are routed to Rx queue 6. For example, if PSRQ6[5] are set, packets with USP field equal to 5 are routed to Rx queue 6. The software must ensure that the content of this field is mutually exclusive to the PSRQ fields for other queues, that is, the same priority is not mapped to multi- ple Rx queues. This field also determines the priorities to be included in the PFC packet sent to re- mote station when Rx queue 6 crosses the flow control threshold settings.         |

All packets with priorities that match the values set in this field are routed to Rx queue 5. For example, if PSRQ5[6] is set, packets with USP field equal to 6 are routed to Rx queue 5. The software must ensure that the content of this field is mutually exclusive to the PSRQ fields for other queues, that is, the same priority is not mapped to multi- ple Rx queues. ## Receive Queue Control 4 Register

The EMAC\_RXQ\_CTL4 register controls the routing of unicast and multicast packets that fail the Destination or Source address filter to the Rx queues.

Figure 30-152: EMAC\_RXQ\_CTL4 Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-207: EMAC\_RXQ\_CTL4 Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|--------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 19:17 (R/W)        | VFFQ       | VLAN Tag Filter Fail Packets Queue. The EMAC_RXQ_CTL4.VFFQ field holds the Rx queue number to which the tagged packets failing the Destination or Source Address filter (and EMAC_RXQ_CTL4.UFFQE / EMAC_RXQ_CTL4.MFFQE = 0) or failing the VLAN tag filter must be routed to. The EMAC_RXQ_CTL4.VFFQ field is valid only when EMAC_RXQ_CTL4.VFFQE = 1.                                                                                                                                                                          |
| 16 (R/W)           | VFFQE      | VLAN Tag Filter Fail Packets Queuing Enable. When the EMAC_RXQ_CTL4.VFFQE bit is set, the tagged packets which fail the Destination or Source address filter or fail the VLAN tag filter, are routed to the Rx queue number programmed in the EMAC_RXQ_CTL4.VFFQ field. When EMAC_RXQ_CTL4.VFFQE = 0, the tagged packets which fail the Destination or Source address filter or fail the VLAN tag filter are routed based on other routing options. The EMAC_RXQ_CTL4.VFFQE bit is valid only when the EMAC_MACPKT_FILT.RA = 1. |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — Receive Flow Control Register

<!-- source: 133_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2311–2312 -->

## Receive Flow Control Register

The EMAC\_RXFLOW\_CTL register controls the pausing of MAC transmit based on the received pause packet.

Figure 30-153: EMAC\_RXFLOW\_CTL Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-208: EMAC\_RXFLOW\_CTL Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
|--------------------|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 8 (R/W)            | PFCE       | Priority Based Flow Control Enable. When the EMAC_RXFLOW_CTL.PFCE bit is set, it enables generation and reception of priority-based flow control (PFC) packets. When EMAC_RXFLOW_CTL.PFCE = 0, it enables generation and reception of 802.3x Pause control packets.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Priority Based Flow Control Enable. When the EMAC_RXFLOW_CTL.PFCE bit is set, it enables generation and reception of priority-based flow control (PFC) packets. When EMAC_RXFLOW_CTL.PFCE = 0, it enables generation and reception of 802.3x Pause control packets.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| 8 (R/W)            | PFCE       | 0                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Priority Based Flow Control is Disabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| 8 (R/W)            | PFCE       | 1                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Priority Based Flow Control is Enabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| 1 (R/W)            | UP         | Unicast Pause Packet Detect. A pause packet is processed when it has the unique multicast address specified in the IEEE 802.3. When the EMAC_RXFLOW_CTL.UP bit is set, the MAC can also detect Pause packets with unicast address of the station. This unicast address should be as specified in EMAC_ADDR0_HI and EMAC_ADDR0_LO. When EMAC_RXFLOW_CTL.UP = 0, the MAC only detects Pause packets with unique multicast address. Note: The MAC does not process a Pause packet if the multicast address is different from the unique multicast address. This is also applicable to the received PFC packet when the Priority Flow Control (PFC) is enabled. The unique multicast address (0x01_80_C2_00_00_01) is as specified in IEEE 802.1 Qbb-2011. | Unicast Pause Packet Detect. A pause packet is processed when it has the unique multicast address specified in the IEEE 802.3. When the EMAC_RXFLOW_CTL.UP bit is set, the MAC can also detect Pause packets with unicast address of the station. This unicast address should be as specified in EMAC_ADDR0_HI and EMAC_ADDR0_LO. When EMAC_RXFLOW_CTL.UP = 0, the MAC only detects Pause packets with unique multicast address. Note: The MAC does not process a Pause packet if the multicast address is different from the unique multicast address. This is also applicable to the received PFC packet when the Priority Flow Control (PFC) is enabled. The unique multicast address (0x01_80_C2_00_00_01) is as specified in IEEE 802.1 Qbb-2011. |
| 1 (R/W)            | UP         | 0                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Unicast Pause Packet Detect Disabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| 1 (R/W)            | UP         | 1                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Unicast Pause Packet Detect Enabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

Table 30-208: EMAC\_RXFLOW\_CTL Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
|--------------------|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 0 (R/W)            | RFE        | Receive Flow Control Enable. When the EMAC_RXFLOW_CTL.RFE bit is set and the MAC is operating in full- duplex mode, the MAC decodes the received Pause packet and disables its transmitter for a specified (Pause) time. When EMAC_RXFLOW_CTL.RFE = 0 or the MAC is operating in half-duplex mode, the decode function of the Pause packet is disabled. When PFC is enabled, flow control is enabled for PFC packets. The MAC decodes the received PFC packet and disables the Transmit queue, with matching priorities, for a duration of received Pause time. 0 Receive Flow Control is Disabled |
| 0 (R/W)            | RFE        | 1 Receive Flow Control is Enabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| 0 (R/W)            | RFE        |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
