## Receive Transmit Status Register

The EMAC\_RXTX\_STAT register contains the receive and transmit error status.

Figure 30-154: EMAC\_RXTX\_STAT Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-209: EMAC\_RXTX\_STAT Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|--------------------|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 8 (R/NW)           | RWT        | Receive Watchdog Timeout. The EMAC_RXTX_STAT.RWT bit is set when a packet with length greater than 2,048 bytes is received (10, 240 bytes when jumbo packet mode is enabled (EMAC_MAC_CFG.JE = 1) and EMAC_MAC_CFG.WD = 0. The EMAC_RXTX_STAT.RWT bit is set when a packet with length greater than 16,383 bytes is received and EMAC_MAC_CFG.WD = 1. Access restriction applies. Clears on read (or write of 1 when EMAC_CSR_SW_CTL.RCWE = 1). Self-set to 1 on internal event. 0 No Receive Watchdog Timeout | Receive Watchdog Timeout. The EMAC_RXTX_STAT.RWT bit is set when a packet with length greater than 2,048 bytes is received (10, 240 bytes when jumbo packet mode is enabled (EMAC_MAC_CFG.JE = 1) and EMAC_MAC_CFG.WD = 0. The EMAC_RXTX_STAT.RWT bit is set when a packet with length greater than 16,383 bytes is received and EMAC_MAC_CFG.WD = 1. Access restriction applies. Clears on read (or write of 1 when EMAC_CSR_SW_CTL.RCWE = 1). Self-set to 1 on internal event. 0 No Receive Watchdog Timeout |
| 5 (R/NW)           | EXCOL      | Excessive Collisions. When EMAC_MTL_OPMODE.DTXSTS = 1, the EMAC_RXTX_STAT.EXCOL bit indicates that the transmission aborted after 16 successive collisions while attempt- ing to transmit the current packet. When EMAC_MAC_CFG.DR = 1, the EMAC_RXTX_STAT.EXCOL bit is set after the first collision and the packet trans- mission is aborted. Access restriction applies. Clears on read (or write of 1 when EMAC_CSR_SW_CTL.RCWE = 1). Self-set to 1 on internal event.                                     | Excessive Collisions. When EMAC_MTL_OPMODE.DTXSTS = 1, the EMAC_RXTX_STAT.EXCOL bit indicates that the transmission aborted after 16 successive collisions while attempt- ing to transmit the current packet. When EMAC_MAC_CFG.DR = 1, the EMAC_RXTX_STAT.EXCOL bit is set after the first collision and the packet trans- mission is aborted. Access restriction applies. Clears on read (or write of 1 when EMAC_CSR_SW_CTL.RCWE = 1). Self-set to 1 on internal event.                                     |
| 5 (R/NW)           | EXCOL      | 0                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | No Collision                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| 5 (R/NW)           | EXCOL      | 1                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Excessive Collision is Sensed                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

Table 30-209: EMAC\_RXTX\_STAT Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|--------------------|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 4 (R/NW)           | LCOL       | Late Collision. When EMAC_MTL_OPMODE.DTXSTS = 1, the EMAC_RXTX_STAT.LCOL bit indicates that the packet transmission aborted because a collision occurred after the collision window (64 bytes including Preamble in MII mode; 512 bytes including Pre- amble and Carrier Extension in GMII mode). The EMAC_RXTX_STAT.LCOL bit is not valid if the Underflow error occurs. Access restriction applies. Clears on read (or write of 1 when EMAC_CSR_SW_CTL.RCWE = 1). Self-set to 1 on internal event. |
| 3 (R/NW)           | EXDEF      | Excessive Deferral. When EMAC_MTL_OPMODE.DTXSTS = 1 and EMAC_MAC_CFG.DC = 1, the EMAC_RXTX_STAT.EXDEF bit indicates that the transmission ended because of ex- cessive deferral of over 24,288 bit times (155,680 in 1000/2500 Mbps mode or when jumbo packet mode is enabled (EMAC_MAC_CFG.JE = 1)). Access restriction applies. Clears on read (or write of 1 when EMAC_CSR_SW_CTL.RCWE = 1). Self-set to 1 on internal event. 0 No Excessive Deferral                                             |
| 2 (R/NW)           | LCARR      | 1 Excessive Deferral Loss of Carrier. When EMAC_MTL_OPMODE.DTXSTS = 1, the EMAC_RXTX_STAT.LCARR bit indicates that the loss of carrier occurred during packet transmission, that is, the ETHx_CRS signal was inactive for one or more transmission clock periods during packet transmission. The EMAC_RXTX_STAT.LCARR bit is valid only for packets transmitted without collision. Access restriction applies. Clears on read (or write of 1 when                                                    |
|                    |            | 0 Carrier is Present                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| 1 (R/NW)           | NCARR      | No Carrier. When EMAC_MTL_OPMODE.DTXSTS = 1, the EMAC_RXTX_STAT.NCARR bit indicates that the carrier signal from the PHY is not present at the end of preamble transmission. Access restriction applies. Clears on read (or write of 1 when EMAC_CSR_SW_CTL.RCWE = 1). Self-set to 1 on internal event.                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| 1 (R/NW)           |            | 0 Carrier is Present                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| 1 (R/NW)           |            | 1 No Carrier                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| 1 (R/NW)           |            |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

The EMAC_RXTX_STAT.TJT bit indicates that the Transmit Jabber Timer expired which happens when the packet size exceeds 2,048 bytes (10,240 bytes when jumbo packet mode is enabled (EMAC_MAC_CFG.JE = 1) and EMAC_MAC_CFG.JD = 0. # Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — Subsecond Increment Register

<!-- source: 138_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2319–2319 -->

## Subsecond Increment Register

The EMAC\_TM\_SUBSEC register specifies the value to be added to the internal system time register every cycle of PTP clock.

Figure 30-158: EMAC\_TM\_SUBSEC Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-213: EMAC\_TM\_SUBSEC Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|--------------------|------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 23:16 (R/W)        | SSINC      | Sub-second Increment Value. The value programmed in the EMAC_TM_SUBSEC.SSINC field is accumulated ev- ery PTP clock cycle with the contents of the sub-second register. For example, when the PTP clock is 50 MHz (period is 20 ns), program 20 (0x14) when the EMAC_TM_NSEC register has an accuracy of 1 ns (EMAC_TM_CTL.TSCTRLSSR = 1). When EMAC_TM_CTL.TSCTRLSSR = 0, the EMAC_TM_NSEC register has a resolution of ~0.465 ns. In this case, program a value of 43 (0x2B) which is derived by 20 ns/0.465. |
| 15:8 (R/W)         | SNSINC     | Sub-nanosecond Increment Value. The EMAC_TM_SUBSEC.SNSINC field contains the sub-nanosecond increment value, represented in nanoseconds multiplied by 2 8 . This value is accumulated with the sub-nanoseconds field of the subsecond register. For example, when EMAC_TM_CTL.TSCTRLSSR = 1. and if the required incre- ment is 5.3ns, then EMAC_TM_SUBSEC.SSINC should be 0x05 and EMAC_TM_SUBSEC.SNSINC should be 0x4C.                                                                                       |

System Time - Higher Word Seconds register.

The EMAC_TM_HISEC register is optional. Add this register by selecting the Add IEEE 1588 Higher Word Register option. The EMAC_TM_HISEC register is directly written to initialize the value and it is incremented when there is an overflow from 32 bits of the EMAC_TM_SEC register. Access restriction applies. # Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — System Time Nanoseconds Register

<!-- source: 140_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2321–2321 -->

## System Time Nanoseconds Register

The EMAC\_TM\_NSEC register, along with System Time Seconds register, indicates the current value of the system time maintained by the MAC.

Figure 30-160: EMAC\_TM\_NSEC Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-215: EMAC\_TM\_NSEC Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
|--------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 30:0 (R/NW)        | TSSS       | Time Stamp Sub Seconds. The value in the EMAC_TM_NSEC.TSSS field has the sub-second representation of time, with an accuracy of 0.46 ns. (EMAC_TM_CTL.TSCTRLSSR = 1), each bit represents 1 ns. The maximum value is 0x3B9A_C9FF after which it rolls over to zero. |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — System Time Nanoseconds Update Register

<!-- source: 141_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2322–2323 -->

## System Time Nanoseconds Update Register

MAC System Time Nanoseconds Update register.

Figure 30-161: EMAC\_TM\_NSECUPDT Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-216: EMAC\_TM\_NSECUPDT Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|--------------------|------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31 (R/W)           | ADDSUB     | Add or Subtract Time. When the EMAC_TM_NSECUPDT.ADDSUB bit is set, the time value is subtracted with the contents of the update register. When EMAC_TM_NSECUPDT.ADDSUB = 0, the time value is added with the contents of the update register. |
|                    |            | 0 Add Time                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|                    |            | 1 Subtract Time                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

Table 30-216: EMAC\_TM\_NSECUPDT Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|--------------------|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 30:0 (R/W)         | TSSS       | Time Stamp Sub Seconds. The EMAC_TM_NSECUPDT.TSSS field is the sub-seconds part of the update. When EMAC_TM_NSECUPDT.ADDSUB = 1, the EMAC_TM_NSECUPDT.TSSS field must be programmed with the complement of the sub-seconds part of the update value as described. When EMAC_TM_NSECUPDT.ADDSUB = 0, the EMAC_TM_NSECUPDT.TSSS field must be programmed with the sub-seconds part of the update value, with an ac- curacy based on the EMAC_TM_CTL.TSCTRLSSR bit. For EMAC_TM_CTL.TSCTRLSSR = 1: -- The programmed value must be 10 9 - <sub-second value>. -- Each bit represents 1 ns and the programmed value should not exceed 0x3B9A_C9FF. For EMAC_TM_CTL.TSCTRLSSR = 0: -- The programmed value must be 2 31 - <sub-second_value>. -- Each bit represents an accuracy of 0.46 ns. For example, to subtract 2.000000001 seconds from the system time, then the EMAC_TM_NSECUPDT.TSSS field must be 0x7FFF_FFFF (that is, 2 31 - 1), when EMAC_TM_CTL.TSCTRLSSR = 0 and 0x3B9A_C9FF (that is, 10 9 - 1), when EMAC_TM_CTL.TSCTRLSSR = 1. |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — System Time Seconds Register

<!-- source: 142_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2324–2324 -->

## System Time Seconds Register

The EMAC\_TM\_SEC register, along with the EMAC\_TM\_NSEC register, indicates the current value of the system time maintained by the MAC. Though it is updated on a continuous basis, there is some delay from the actual time because of clock domain transfer latencies (from PTP clock to SCLK0).

Figure 30-162: EMAC\_TM\_SEC Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-217: EMAC\_TM\_SEC Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                    |
|--------------------|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:0 (R/NW)        | TSS        | Time Stamp Second. The value in the EMAC_TM_SEC.TSS field indicates the current value in seconds of the System Time maintained by the MAC. |

---

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — System Time Seconds Update Register

<!-- source: 143_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2325–2325 -->

## System Time Seconds Update Register

The EMAC\_TM\_SECUPDT register, along with the EMAC\_TM\_NSECUPDT register, initializes or updates the system time maintained by the MAC. Write both registers before setting the EMAC\_TM\_CTL.TSINIT or EMAC\_TM\_CTL.TSUPDT bits.

Figure 30-163: EMAC\_TM\_SECUPDT Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-218: EMAC\_TM\_SECUPDT Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
|--------------------|------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:0 (R/W)         | TSS        | Time Stamp Seconds. The value in the EMAC_TM_SECUPDT.TSS field is the seconds part of the update. When EMAC_TM_NSECUPDT.ADDSUB = 0, the EMAC_TM_SECUPDT.TSS field must be programmed with the seconds part of the update value. When EMAC_TM_NSECUPDT.ADDSUB = 1, the EMAC_TM_SECUPDT.TSS field must be programmed with the complement of the seconds part of the update val- ue. For example, to subtract 2.000000001 seconds from the system time, the EMAC_TM_SECUPDT.TSS field must be 0xFFFF_FFFE (that is, 2 32 - 2). |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — Time Stamp Addend Register

<!-- source: 144_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2326–2326 -->

## Time Stamp Addend Register

The EMAC\_TM\_ADDEND register value is used only when the system time is configured for Fine Update mode (EMAC\_TM\_CTL.TSCFUPDT). The content of this register is added to a 32-bit accumulator in every clock cycle (PTP clock) and the system time is updated when the accumulator overflows.

Figure 30-164: EMAC\_TM\_ADDEND Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-219: EMAC\_TM\_ADDEND Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                           |
|--------------------|------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:0 (R/W)         | TSAR       | Timestamp Addend Register. The EMAC_TM_ADDEND.TSAR field indicates the 32-bit time value to be added to the Accumulator register to achieve time synchronization. |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — Time Stamp Control Register

<!-- source: 145_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2327–2333 -->

## Time Stamp Control Register

The EMAC\_TM\_CTL register controls the operation of the System Time generator and processing of PTP packets for time stamping in the receiver.

Figure 30-165: EMAC\_TM\_CTL Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-220: EMAC\_TM\_CTL Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name    | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|--------------------|-------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 28 (R/W)           | AV8021ASMEN | AV 802.1AS Mode Enable. When the EMAC_TM_CTL.AV8021ASMEN bit is set, the MAC processes only un- tagged PTP over Ethernet packets for providing PTP status and capturing time stamp snapshots, that is, IEEE 802.1AS mode of operation. When PTP offload feature is enabled, for the purpose of PTP offload, the transport specific field in the PTP header is generated and checked based on the value of the EMAC_TM_CTL.AV8021ASMEN bit. 0 AV 802.1AS Mode is Disabled                                                        |
| 24 (R/W)           | TXTSSTSM    | Transmit Time Stamp Status Mode. When the EMAC_TM_CTL.TXTSSTSM bit is set, the MAC overwrites the earlier transmit time stamp status even if it is not read by the software. The MAC indicates this by setting the EMAC_TXTMSTAT_NSEC.TXTSSMIS bit. When EMAC_TM_CTL.TXTSSTSM = 0, the MAC ignores the time stamp status of current packet if the time stamp status of previous packet is not read by the software. The MAC indicates this by setting the EMAC_TXTMSTAT_NSEC.TXTSSMIS bit. 0 Disable                            |
| 19 (R/W)           | CSC         | Enable Checksum Correction During OST for PTP Over UDP/IPv4 Packets. When the EMAC_TM_CTL.CSC bit is set, the last two bytes of PTP message sent over UDP/IPv4 is updated to keep the UDP checksum correct, for changes made to origin time stamp and/or correction field as part of one step time stamp operation. The application forms the packet with these two dummy bytes. When cleared (=0), no updates are done to keep the UDP checksum correct. The ap- plication forms the packet with UDP checksum configured to 0. |
| 19 (R/W)           | CSC         | 0 Checksum Correction During OST for PTP Over UDP/IPv4 Packets is Disabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| 19 (R/W)           | CSC         | 1 Checksum Correction During OST for PTP Over UDP/IPv4 Packets is Enabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| 19 (R/W)           | CSC         |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

When media clock generation and recovery is enabled the EMAC_PRSNTM_UPDT register must also be updated before setting this field. Access restriction applies. Write 1 to set. Self-cleared. Writing 0 has no effect. |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — Time Stamp Egress Asymmetry Correction Register

<!-- source: 146_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2334–2334 -->

## Time Stamp Egress Asymmetry Correction Register

The EMAC\_TM\_EGASYM\_CORR register contains the egress asymmetry correction value to be used while updating the correction field in PDelay\_Req PTP messages.

Figure 30-166: EMAC\_TM\_EGASYM\_CORR Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-221: EMAC\_TM\_EGASYM\_CORR Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
|--------------------|------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:0 (R/W)         | OSTEAC     | One-Step Time Stamp Egress Asymmetry Correction. The EMAC_TM_EGASYM_CORR.OSTEAC field contains the egress path asymmetry value to be subtracted from correctionField of Pdelay_Resp PTP packet. The program- med value must be the negated value in units of nanoseconds multiplied by 2 16 . For example, if the required correction is +2.5 ns, the programmed value must be 0xFFFD_8000, which is the 2's complement of 0x0002_8000(2.5 * 216). Similarly, if the required correction is -3.3 ns, the programmed value is 0x0003_4CCC (3.3 * 216). |

## Time Stamp Ingress Asymmetry Correction Register

The EMAC\_TM\_INGASYM\_CORR register contains the Ingress Asymmetry Correction value to be used while updating correction field in PDelay\_Resp PTP messages.

Figure 30-170: EMAC\_TM\_INGASYM\_CORR Register Diagram

| 31:0 (R/W)         | OSTIAC     | One-Step Time Stamp Ingress Asymmetry Correction. The EMAC_TM_INGASYM_CORR.OSTIAC field contains the ingress path asymme- try value to be added to correctionField of Pdelay_Resp PTP packet. The programmed value should be in units of nanoseconds and multiplied by 2 16 . For example, 2.5 ns is represented as 0x00028000. The value can also be negative, which is represented in 2's complement form with bit 31 representing the sign bit. |

All bits except bits[27:25] are cleared when the application reads the EMAC\_TM\_STAT register.

A value equal to the selected depth of FIFO (4, 8, or 16) indicates that the Auxiliary Snapshot FIFO is full. These bits are cleared (to 00000) when the Auxiliary snapshot FIFO clear bit is set. The EMAC_TM_STAT.ATSSTN field identifies the auxiliary trigger inputs for which the time stamp available in the Auxiliary Snapshot Register is applicable. When more than one bit is set at the same time, it means that corresponding auxiliary triggers were sampled at the same clock. These bits are applicable only if the number of auxiliary snapshots is more than one. One bit is assigned for each trigger as shown in the follow- ing list: - Bit 16: Auxiliary trigger 0 - Bit 17: Auxiliary trigger 1 - Bit 18: Auxiliary trigger 2 - Bit 19: Auxiliary trigger 3 The software can read this register to find the triggers that are set when the time stamp is taken. |

The EMAC_TM_STAT.TXTSSIS bit is cleared when the EMAC_TXTMSTAT_SEC register is read (or write to EMAC_TXTMSTAT_SEC register when EMAC_CSR_SW_CTL.RCWE = 1). 0 Status Not Detected 1 Status Detected                                       |

## Transmit Queue Priority Mapping 0 Register

The EMAC\_TXQ\_PRTY\_MAP0 register contains the priority values assigned to Tx queue 0 through Tx queue 3.

Figure 30-175: EMAC\_TXQ\_PRTY\_MAP0 Register Diagram

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — Transmit Time Stamp Status Nanoseconds Register

<!-- source: 157_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2350–2350 -->

## Transmit Time Stamp Status Nanoseconds Register

The EMAC\_TXTMSTAT\_NSEC register contains the nanosecond part of time stamp captured for transmit packets when Tx status is disabled. The EMAC\_TXTMSTAT\_NSEC register, along with EMAC\_TXTMSTAT\_SEC, gives the 64-bit time stamp captured for the PTP packet successfully transmitted by the MAC. This value is considered to be read by the application when the last byte of the EMAC\_TXTMSTAT\_NSEC register is read. In the little-endian mode, this means when bits[31:24] are read; in big-endian mode, bits[7:0] are read. If the application does not read these registers and time stamp of another packet is captured, then either the current time stamp is lost (overwritten) or the new time stamp is lost (dropped), depending on the configuration of the EMAC\_TM\_CTL.TXTSSTSM bit. The status bit EMAC\_TM\_STAT.TXTSSIS is set when the MAC transmitter captures the time stamp.

Figure 30-177: EMAC\_TXTMSTAT\_NSEC Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-232: EMAC\_TXTMSTAT\_NSEC Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|--------------------|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31 (R/NW)          | TXTSSMIS   | Transmit Time Stamp Status Missed. When the EMAC_TXTMSTAT_NSEC.TXTSSMIS bit is set, it indicates one of the following: The time stamp of the current packet is ignored if EMAC_TM_CTL.TXTSSTSM = 0. The time stamp of the previous packet is overwritten with time stamp of the current packet if EMAC_TM_CTL.TXTSSTSM = 1. Access restriction applies. Clears on read. Self-set to 1 on internal event. 0 Status Not Detected |
| 30:0 (R/NW)        | TXTSSLO    | Transmit Time Stamp Status Low. The EMAC_TXTMSTAT_NSEC.TXTSSLO field contains the 31 bits of the nanosec- onds field of the transmit packet's captured time stamp.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — VLAN Hash Table Register

<!-- source: 159_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2352–2352 -->

## VLAN Hash Table Register

When EMAC\_VLANTAG\_CTL.VTHM = 1, the 16-bit EMAC\_VLAN\_HASHTBL register is used for group address filtering based on the VLAN tag. For hash filtering, the content of the 16-bit VLAN tag or 12-bit VLAN ID (based on EMAC\_VLANTAG\_CTL.ETV) in the incoming packet is passed through the CRC logic. The upper four bits of the calculated hash value are used to index the contents of the VLAN hash table. For example, hash value of 4b'1000 selects bit 8 of the VLAN hash table.

The hash value of the destination address is calculated in the following way:

1. Calculate the 32-bit CRC for the VLAN tag or ID (For steps to calculate CRC32, see Section 3.2.8 of IEEE 802.3).
2. Perform bitwise reversal for the value obtained in step 1.
3. Take the upper four bits from the value obtained in step 2. The VLAN hash table register is configured to be double-synchronized to the (G)MII clock domain, the synchronization is triggered only when bits[15:8] (in littleendian mode) or bits[7:0] (in big-endian mode) of this register are written.

Consecutive writes to this register should be performed after at least four clock cycles in the (G)MII clock domain.

Figure 30-179: EMAC\_VLAN\_HASHTBL Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-234: EMAC\_VLAN\_HASHTBL Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                               |
|--------------------|------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 15:0               | VLHT       | VLAN Hash Table.                                                      |
| (R/W)              |            | The EMAC_VLAN_HASHTBL.VLHT field contains the 16-bit VLAN Hash Table. |

## VLAN Tag Indirect Access Data Register

The EMAC\_VLANTAG\_DAT register holds the read/write data for Indirect Access of the Per VLAN Tag registers. During the read access, this field contains valid read data only after the OB bit is reset. During the write access, this field should be valid prior to EMAC\_VLANTAG\_CTL.OB = 1

If the routing is not based on the VLAN tag filter, this field does not need to be pro- grammed.                                        |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — MMC Receive FPE Interrupt Status Register

<!-- source: 165_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2369–2370 -->

## MMC Receive FPE Interrupt Status Register

The EMAC\_MMC\_FPE\_RXINT register maintains the interrupts generated from all FPE-related receive statistics counters. The EMAC\_MMC\_FPE\_RXINT register maintains the interrupts generated when transmit statistic counters reach half their maximum values (0x8000\_0000 for the 32-bit counter and 0x8000 for 16-bit counter), and when they cross their maximum values (0xFFFF\_FFFF for 32-bit counter and 0xFFFF for 16-bit counter). When the Counter Stop Rollover is set, the interrupts are set but the counter remains at all-ones.

The EMAC\_MMC\_FPE\_RXINT register is a 32-bit register. An interrupt bit is cleared when the respective MMC counter that caused the interrupt is read. The least significant byte lane (Bits[7:0]) of the respective counter must be read to clear the interrupt bit.

<!-- image -->

## MMC Receive FPE Interrupt Mask Register

The EMAC\_MMC\_FPE\_RXIMSK register maintains the masks for interrupts generated from all FPE-related receive statistics counters. The EMAC\_MMC\_RXIMSK register maintains the masks for the interrupts generated when FPE-related receive statistic counters reach half of their maximum value or the maximum values. The EMAC\_MMC\_FPE\_RXIMSK register is 32 bit wide.

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — MMC Transmit FPE Interrupt Status Register

<!-- source: 167_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2373–2374 -->

## MMC Transmit FPE Interrupt Status Register

The EMAC\_MMC\_FPE\_TXINT register maintains the interrupts generated from all FPE related T ransmit statistics counters. The MMC FPE Transmit Interrupt register maintains the interrupts generated when transmit statistic counters reach half their maximum values (0x8000\_0000 for 32 bit counter and 0x8000 for 16 bit counter), and when they cross their maximum values (0xFFFF\_FFFF for 32-bit counter and 0xFFFF for 16-bit counter). When Counter Stop Rollover is set, the interrupts are set but the counter remains at all-ones. The MMC FPE Transmit Interrupt register is a 32 bit register. An interrupt bit is cleared when the respective MMC counter that caused the interrupt is read. The least significant byte lane (Bits[7:0]) of the respective counter must be read to clear the interrupt bit.

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — MMC Receive IPC Interrupt Status Register

<!-- source: 169_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2376–2384 -->

## MMC Receive IPC Interrupt Status Register

The EMAC\_MMC\_IPC\_RXINT register maintains the interrupt that the receive IPC statistic counters generate.

The EMAC\_MMC\_IPC\_RXINT register maintains the interrupts generated when receive IPC statistic counters reach half their maximum values (0x8000\_0000 for 32 bit counter and 0x8000 for 16 bit counter), and when they cross their maximum values (0xFFFF\_FFFF for 32 bit counter and 0xFFFF for 16 bit counter). When Counter Stop Rollover is set, the interrupts are set but the counter remains at all-ones.

The EMAC\_MMC\_IPC\_RXINT register is 32 bit wide. When the MMC IPC counter that caused the interrupt is read, its corresponding interrupt bit is cleared. The counter's least-significant byte lane (Bits[7:0]) must be read to clear the interrupt bit.

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — MMC Receive IPC Interrupt Mask Register

<!-- source: 170_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2385–2393 -->

## MMC Receive IPC Interrupt Mask Register

The EMAC\_MMC\_IPC\_RXIMSK register maintains the mask for the interrupt generated from the receive IPC statistic counters.

The MMC Receive Checksum Off load Interrupt Mask register maintains the masks for the interrupts generated when the receive IPC (Checksum Off load) statistic counters reach half their maximum value, and when they reach their maximum values. The EMAC\_MMC\_IPC\_RXIMSK register is 32 bits wide.

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — MMC Receive FPE Fragment Counter Register

## MMC Receive FPE Fragment Counter Register

The EMAC\_RXFPE\_FRGMNT\_CNT register provides the number of additional mPackets received due to preemption.

| 31:0 (R/NW)        | FFC        | Rx FPE Fragment Counter. The EMAC_RXFPE_FRGMNT_CNT.FFC field indicates the number of additional mPackets received due to preemption. Exists when at least one of the RX/TX MMCcounters are enabled during an FPE- enabled configuration. |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — MMC Receive Interrupt Status Register

<!-- source: 172_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2395–2403 -->

## MMC Receive Interrupt Status Register

The EMAC\_MMC\_RXINT register maintains the interrupts generated from all receive statistics counters when the following occurs:

Receive statistic counters reach half of their maximum values (0x8000\_0000 for 32-bit counter and 0x8000 for 16bit counter).

Receive statistic counters cross their maximum values (0xFFFF\_FFFF for 32-bit counter and 0xFFFF for 16-bit counter).

When the Counter Stop Rollover is set, interrupts are set but the counter remains at all-ones. The EMAC\_MMC\_RXINT register is a 32 bit register. An interrupt bit is cleared when the respective MMC counter that caused the interrupt is read. The least significant byte lane (Bits[7:0]) of the respective counter must be read to clear the interrupt bit.

Note: R\_SS\_RC means that this register bit is set internally, and it is cleared when the counter register is read.

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — MMC Receive Interrupt Mask Register

<!-- source: 173_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2404–2412 -->

## MMC Receive Interrupt Mask Register

The EMAC\_MMC\_RXIMSK register maintains the masks for the interrupts generated when receive statistic counters reach half of their maximum value or the maximum values.

The EMAC\_MMC\_RXIMSK register is 32 bit wide.

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — MMC Receive FPE Packet Assembly Error Counter Register

<!-- source: 174_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2413–2413 -->

## MMC Receive FPE Packet Assembly Error Counter Register

The EMAC\_RXPKT\_ASERR\_CNT register provides the number of MAC frames with reassembly errors on the receiver, due to mismatch in the fragment count value.

Figure 30-194: EMAC\_RXPKT\_ASERR\_CNT Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-249: EMAC\_RXPKT\_ASERR\_CNT Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|--------------------|------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:0 (R/NW)        | PAEC       | Rx Packet Assembly Error Counter. The EMAC_RXPKT_ASERR_CNT.PAEC field indicates the number of MAC frames with reassembly errors on the receiver, due to mismatch in the Fragment Count value. Exists when any one of the RX/TX MMCcounters are enabled during an FPE-ena- bled configuration. |

The EMAC_RXPKT_SMDERR_CNT.PSEC field indicates the number of MAC frames rejected due to unknown SMD value and MAC frame fragments rejected due to arriving with an SMD-C when there was no preceding preempted frame. Exists when at least one of the RX/TX MMCcounters are enabled during an FPE-enabled configuration. |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — MMC Transmit Interrupt Status Register

<!-- source: 179_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2418–2426 -->

## MMC Transmit Interrupt Status Register

The EMAC\_MMC\_TXINT register maintains the interrupts generated from all transmit statistics counters when transmit statistic counters reach half their maximum values (0x8000\_0000 for 32 bit counter and 0x8000 for 16 bit counter), and when they cross their maximum values (0xFFFF\_FFFF for 32-bit counter and 0xFFFF for 16-bit counter).

When Counter Stop Rollover is set, the interrupts are set but the counter remains at all-ones.

The EMAC\_MMC\_TXINT register is a 32-bit register. An interrupt bit is cleared when the respective MMC counter that caused the interrupt is read.

The least significant byte lane (bits[7:0]) of the respective counter must be read to clear the interrupt bit.

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — MMC Transmit Interrupt Mask Register

<!-- source: 180_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2427–2435 -->

## MMC Transmit Interrupt Mask Register

The EMAC\_MMC\_TXIMSK register maintains the masks for interrupts generated from all transmit statistics counters.

The EMAC\_MMC\_TXIMSK register maintains the masks for the interrupts generated when the transmit statistic counters reach half of their maximum value or the maximum values. The EMAC\_MMC\_TXIMSK register is 32 bits wide.

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — EST Control Register

<!-- source: 181_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2436–2438 -->

## EST Control Register

The EMAC\_EST\_CTL register controls the operation of Enhancements to Scheduled Transmission (EST) (IEEE802.1Qbv).

Figure 30-201: EMAC\_EST\_CTL Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-256: EMAC\_EST\_CTL Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|--------------------|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:24 (R/W)        | PTOV       | PTP Time Offset Value. The EMAC_EST_CTL.PTOV field indicates the value of the PTP clock period multi- plied by 6 in nanoseconds. This value is needed to avoid transmission overruns at the beginning of the installation of a new GCL.                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| 23:12 (R/W)        | CTOV       | Current Time Offset Value. The EMAC_EST_CTL.CTOV field provides a 12 bit time offset value in nano second that is added to the current time to compensate for all the implementation pipeline delays such as the CDC sync delay, buffering delays, data path delays and so on. This offset helps to ensure that the impact of gate controls is visible on the line exactly at the pre-determined schedule (or as close to the schedule as possible). |

Table 30-256: EMAC\_EST\_CTL Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|--------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 10:8 (R/W)         | TILS       | Time Interval Left Shift Amount. The EMAC_EST_CTL.TILS field provides the left shift amount for the program- med time interval values used in the Gate Control Lists. - 000: No left shift needed (equal to x1ns) - 001: Left shift TI by 1 bit (equal to x2ns) - 010: Left shift TI by 2 bits (equal to x4ns) - ... - ... - 100: Left shift TI by 7 bits (equal to x128ns) Based on the configuration one or more bits of this field should be treated as reserved/ read-only. | Time Interval Left Shift Amount. The EMAC_EST_CTL.TILS field provides the left shift amount for the program- med time interval values used in the Gate Control Lists. - 000: No left shift needed (equal to x1ns) - 001: Left shift TI by 1 bit (equal to x2ns) - 010: Left shift TI by 2 bits (equal to x4ns) - ... - ... - 100: Left shift TI by 7 bits (equal to x128ns) Based on the configuration one or more bits of this field should be treated as reserved/ read-only. |
| 7:6 (R/W)          | LCSE       | Loop Count to Report Scheduling Error. The EMAC_EST_CTL.LCSE field indicates a programmable number of GCL list iterations before reporting the EMAC_EST_STAT.HLBS bit.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Loop Count to Report Scheduling Error. The EMAC_EST_CTL.LCSE field indicates a programmable number of GCL list iterations before reporting the EMAC_EST_STAT.HLBS bit.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| 7:6 (R/W)          | LCSE       | 0                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | 4 Iterations                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| 7:6 (R/W)          | LCSE       | 1                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | 8 Iterations                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| 7:6 (R/W)          | LCSE       | 2                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | 16 Iterations                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| 7:6 (R/W)          | LCSE       | 3                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | 32 Iterations                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| 5 (R/W)            | DFBS       | Drop Frames Causing Scheduling Error. When the EMAC_EST_CTL.DFBS bit is set (=1), frames reported to cause HOL blocking due to not getting scheduled (EMAC_EST_STAT.HLBS) after 4,8,16,32 (based on LCSE field of this register) GCL iterations are dropped.                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Drop Frames Causing Scheduling Error. When the EMAC_EST_CTL.DFBS bit is set (=1), frames reported to cause HOL blocking due to not getting scheduled (EMAC_EST_STAT.HLBS) after 4,8,16,32 (based on LCSE field of this register) GCL iterations are dropped.                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| 5 (R/W)            | DFBS       | 0                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Do Not Drop Frames Causing Scheduling Error                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| 5 (R/W)            | DFBS       | 1                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Drop Frames Causing Scheduling Error                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| 4 (R/W)            | DDBF       | Do Not Drop Frames During Frame Size Error. When the EMAC_EST_CTL.DDBF bit is set (=1), frames are not dropped during head-of-line blocking due to a frame size error (EMAC_EST_STAT.HLBF).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Do Not Drop Frames During Frame Size Error. When the EMAC_EST_CTL.DDBF bit is set (=1), frames are not dropped during head-of-line blocking due to a frame size error (EMAC_EST_STAT.HLBF).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| 4 (R/W)            | DDBF       | 0                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Drop Frames During Frame Size Error                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| 4 (R/W)            | DDBF       | 1                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Do Not Drop Frames During Frame Size Error                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

Table 30-256: EMAC\_EST\_CTL Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|--------------------|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1 (R/W)            | SSWL       | Switch to S/W Owned List. When set (=1), the EMAC_EST_CTL.SSWL bit indicates that the software has pro- grammed that list that it currently owns (EMAC_EST_STAT.SWOL) and the hard- ware should switch to the new list based on the new BTR. Hardware clears the EMAC_EST_CTL.SSWL bit when the switch to the EMAC_EST_STAT.SWOL bit happens to indicate the completion of the switch or a BTR error (EMAC_EST_STAT.BTRE = 1). When EMAC_EST_STAT.BTRE = 1, the EMAC_EST_CTL.SSWL bit is cleared, but EMAC_EST_STAT.SWOL is not updat- ed as the switch was not successful. Access restriction applies. Write 1 to set. Self-cleared. Writing 0 has no effect. | Switch to S/W Owned List. When set (=1), the EMAC_EST_CTL.SSWL bit indicates that the software has pro- grammed that list that it currently owns (EMAC_EST_STAT.SWOL) and the hard- ware should switch to the new list based on the new BTR. Hardware clears the EMAC_EST_CTL.SSWL bit when the switch to the EMAC_EST_STAT.SWOL bit happens to indicate the completion of the switch or a BTR error (EMAC_EST_STAT.BTRE = 1). When EMAC_EST_STAT.BTRE = 1, the EMAC_EST_CTL.SSWL bit is cleared, but EMAC_EST_STAT.SWOL is not updat- ed as the switch was not successful. Access restriction applies. Write 1 to set. Self-cleared. Writing 0 has no effect. |
| 0 (R/W)            | EEST       | Enable EST. When set (=1), the EMAC_EST_CTL.EEST bit enables EST. It must be set for the hardware to start processing the gate control lists. When cleared, the gate control list processing is halted and all gates are assumed to be in the Open state. During the tog- gle from 0 to 1, the gate control list processing starts only after EMAC_EST_CTL.SSWL =1.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Enable EST. When set (=1), the EMAC_EST_CTL.EEST bit enables EST. It must be set for the hardware to start processing the gate control lists. When cleared, the gate control list processing is halted and all gates are assumed to be in the Open state. During the tog- gle from 0 to 1, the gate control list processing starts only after EMAC_EST_CTL.SSWL =1.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| 0 (R/W)            | EEST       | 0                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | EST is Disabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| 0 (R/W)            | EEST       | 1                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | EST is Enabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

## EST Extended Control Register

The EMAC\_EST\_EXT\_CTL register indicates the number of overhead bytes for EST related scheduling.

Figure 30-202: EMAC\_EST\_EXT\_CTL Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-257: EMAC\_EST\_EXT\_CTL Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                    |
|--------------------|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 5:0 (R/W)          | OVHD       | Overhead Bytes Value. The EMAC_EST_EXT_CTL.OVHD field indicates the fixed overhead for every pack- et to account for EST Scheduler Delay, IPG or EIPG, and Preamble bytes. |
