# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — EST Frame Size Capture Register

<!-- source: 183_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2440–2440 -->

## EST Frame Size Capture Register

The EMAC\_EST\_FRMSZ\_CAP register captures the frame size and queue number of the first occurrence of the frame size-related error. Upon clearing, it captures the data of immediate next occurrence of a similar error.

Figure 30-203: EMAC\_EST\_FRMSZ\_CAP Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-258: EMAC\_EST\_FRMSZ\_CAP Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|--------------------|------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 18:16 (R/NW)       | HBFQ       | Queue Number of HLBF. The EMAC_EST_FRMSZ_CAP.HBFQ field indicates the binary value of the of the first queue (number) experiencing HLBF error (see HLBF field of status register). Val- ue once written is not altered by any subsequent queue errors of similar nature. Once cleared the queue number of the next occurring HLBF error is captured. The width is based on the number of Tx queues configured; remaining bits are read- only. The EMAC_EST_FRMSZ_CAP.HBFQ field is cleared when the EMAC_EST_FRMSZ_ERR register is all zeros. |
| 14:0 (R/NW)        | HBFS       | Frame Size of HLBF. The EMAC_EST_FRMSZ_CAP.HBFS field indicates the frame size of the dropped frame related to queue number indicated in EMAC_EST_FRMSZ_CAP.HBFQ field. The contents of the register is considered invalid, if the EMAC_EST_FRMSZ_CAP.HBFS field is zero. The EMAC_EST_FRMSZ_CAP.HBFS field cleared when the EMAC_EST_FRMSZ_ERR register is all zeros.                                                                                                                                                                        |

---

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — EST Frame Size Error Register

<!-- source: 184_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2441–2441 -->

## EST Frame Size Error Register

The EMAC\_EST\_FRMSZ\_ERR register provides the one hot encoded queue numbers that are having the frame size-related error.

Figure 30-204: EMAC\_EST\_FRMSZ\_ERR Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-259: EMAC\_EST\_FRMSZ\_ERR Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|--------------------|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 7:0 (R/W)          | FEQN       | Frame Size Error Queue Number. The EMAC_EST_FRMSZ_ERR.FEQN field indicates the one hot encoded queue numbers that have experienced the error described in the HLBF field of status register. Access restriction applies. Self-set to 1 on internal event. Write 1 to clear. Writing 0 has no effect. |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — EST Gate Control List Control Register

<!-- source: 185_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2442–2444 -->

## EST Gate Control List Control Register

The EMAC\_EST\_GCL\_CTL register provides the control information for reading/writing to the gate control lists.

Figure 30-205: EMAC\_EST\_GCL\_CTL Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-260: EMAC\_EST\_GCL\_CTL Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|--------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 15:8 (R/W)         | ADDR       | Gate Control List Address. When set (=1), the EMAC_EST_GCL_CTL.ADDR field indicates the address (row number) of the GCL at which the R/W operation must be performed. By default, the GCL pointed by EMAC_EST_STAT.SWOL is selected for R/W. However, if EMAC_EST_GCL_CTL.DBGM =1, a debug mode access is given to R/W from EMAC_EST_GCL_CTL.DBGB . The width of this field is dependent on DWC_EQOS_EST_DEP; unused bits should be treated as read only. Gate Control List Related Registers Address: (GCRA when GCRR =1). By default, the GCL-related register set pointed by EMAC_EST_STAT.SWOL is se- lected for R/W. However, if EMAC_EST_GCL_CTL.DBGM =1, debug mode access is given to R/W from EMAC_EST_GCL_CTL.DBGB . Lower 3 bits are only used in this mode, higher order bits are treated as dont care. 000: BTR Low (31:0) 001: BTR High (63:31) 010: CTR Low (31:0) 011: CTR High (39:32) 100: TER (31:0) 101: LLR (8:0) Others: Reserved |

| 5 (R/W)            | DBGB       | Debug Mode Bank Select. When the EMAC_EST_GCL_CTL.DBGB bit is cleared (=0), it indicates R/W in de- bug mode is directed to bank 0 (GCL0 and corresponding time-related registers). When set (=1), the EMAC_EST_GCL_CTL.DBGB bit indicates R/W in debug mode should be directed to bank 1 (GCL1 and corresponding time-related registers). This value is used when EMAC_EST_GCL_CTL.DBGB = 1 and overrides by value of SWOL (which is normally used). |
| 4 (R/W)            | DBGM       | 1 R/W in Debug Mode Should Be Directed to Bank 1 Debug Mode. When set (=1), the EMAC_EST_GCL_CTL.DBGM bit indicates R/W in debug mode where the memory bank (for GCL and time related registers) is explicitly provided by DBGB value. When the EMAC_EST_GCL_CTL.DBGM bit is cleared (=0), the SWOL bit is used to determine which bank to use.                                                                                                       |
| 2 (R/W)            | GCRR       | 1 Debug Mode is Enabled Gate Control Related Registers. When set (=1), the bit indicates that the R/W access is for the GCL related registers (BTR, CTR, TER, LLR) whose address is provided by GCRA. When cleared (=0), the bit indicates that the R/W is directed to GCL from the address provided by GCLA. 0 Gate Control Related Registers are Disabled 1 Gate Control Related Registers are Enabled                                              |
| 1 (R/W)            | R1W0       | Read/Write Operation. The EMAC_EST_GCL_CTL.R1W0 bit indicates a read or write operation. 0 Write Operation                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

When the EMAC_EST_IEN.CGCE bit is cleared (= 0), an interrupt is not generated.                   | Interrupt Enable for CGCE. When the EMAC_EST_IEN.CGCE bit is set (=1), an interrupt is generated when the constant gate control error occurs and is indicated in the status. # Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — EST Scheduling Error Register

<!-- source: 188_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2448–2448 -->

## EST Scheduling Error Register

The EMAC\_EST\_SCH\_ERR register provides the one hot encoded queue numbers that are having the schedulingrelated error (timeout).

Figure 30-208: EMAC\_EST\_SCH\_ERR Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-263: EMAC\_EST\_SCH\_ERR Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|--------------------|------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 7:0 (R/W)          | SEQN       | Schedule Error Queue Number. The EMAC_EST_SCH_ERR.SEQN field indicates the one hot encoded queue num- bers that have experienced error/timeout described in EMAC_EST_STAT.HLBS field. Access restriction applies. Self-set to 1 on internal event. Write 1 to clear. Writing 0 has no effect. |

## EST Status Register

The EMAC\_EST\_STAT register provides status information related to Enhancements to Scheduled T ransmission (EST) (IEEE802.1Qbv).

<!-- image -->

Current GCL Slot Number

Figure 30-209: EMAC\_EST\_STAT Register Diagram

Table 30-264: EMAC\_EST\_STAT Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|--------------------|------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 19:16 (R/NW)       | CGSN       | Current GCL Slot Number. The EMAC_EST_STAT.CGSN field indicates the slot number of the GCL list. Slot number is a modulo 16 count of the GCL list loops executed so far. Even if a new GCL list is installed, the count is incremental.                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| 15:8 (R/NW)        | BTRL       | BTR Error Loop Count. The EMAC_EST_STAT.BTRL field provides the minimum count (N) for which the equation Current Time =< New BTR + (N * New Cycle Time) becomes true.N= "11111111" indicates the iterations exceeded the value of 128 and the hardware was not able to update New BTR to be equal to or greater than Current Time. Software intervention is needed to update the new BTR. Value is cleared when EMAC_EST_STAT.BTRE = 0. |

When set (=1), the EMAC_EST_STAT.SWOL bit indicates that Gate Control list "1" is owned by the software. Any reads/writes by the software (using indirect access through GCL_Con- trol) is directed to the list indicated by this value by default. The inverse of this value is treated as HWOL. R/W operations performed by hardware are directed to the list pointed by HWOLby default.                                                                                                                                                                  | S/W Owned List. When the EMAC_EST_STAT.SWOL bit is cleared (=0), it indicates that the gate con- trol list number "0" is owned by software. When set (=1), the EMAC_EST_STAT.SWOL bit indicates that Gate Control list "1" is owned by the software. Any reads/writes by the software (using indirect access through GCL_Con- trol) is directed to the list indicated by this value by default. The inverse of this value is treated as HWOL. R/W operations performed by hardware are directed to the list pointed by HWOLby default.                                                                                                                                                                  |
| 7 (R/NW)           | SWOL       | 0                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Gate Control List Number "0" is Owned by Software                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

When set (=1), the EMAC_EST_STAT.CGCE bit indicates that an error occurs when the list length (LLR) is 1 and the Cycle Time (CTR) is less than or equal to the pro- grammed Time Interval (TI) value after the optional left shifting. This implies that gates are either always closed or always open based on the Gate Control values; the same effect can be achieved by other simpler (non TSN) programming mechanisms. Since the implementation does not support such a programming an error is reported. Access restriction applies. Self-set to 1 on internal event. Write 1 to clear. Writing 0 has no effect. | 1 Gate Control List Number "1" is Owned by Software Constant Gate Control Error. When set (=1), the EMAC_EST_STAT.CGCE bit indicates that an error occurs when the list length (LLR) is 1 and the Cycle Time (CTR) is less than or equal to the pro- grammed Time Interval (TI) value after the optional left shifting. This implies that gates are either always closed or always open based on the Gate Control values; the same effect can be achieved by other simpler (non TSN) programming mechanisms. Since the implementation does not support such a programming an error is reported. Access restriction applies. Self-set to 1 on internal event. Write 1 to clear. Writing 0 has no effect. |

Indi- cates to software a potential programming error. The one hot encoded values of the queue numbers that are not able to make progress are indicated in the EMAC_EST_SCH_ERR register. The bit is cleared when the EMAC_EST_SCH_ERR register is all zeros.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Head-Of-Line Blocking Due to Scheduling. When set (=1), the EMAC_EST_STAT.HLBS bit indicates when the frame is not able to win arbitration and get scheduled even after four iterations of the GCL. Indi- cates to software a potential programming error. The one hot encoded values of the queue numbers that are not able to make progress are indicated in the EMAC_EST_SCH_ERR register. The bit is cleared when the EMAC_EST_SCH_ERR register is all zeros.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

When set (=1), the EMAC_EST_STAT.HLBF bit indicates HOL Blocking is noticed on one or more queues as a result of none of the time intervals of gate open in the GCL being greater than or equal to the duration needed for frame size (or frame frag- ment size when preemption is enabled) transmission. # Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — Frame Preemption Advance Register

<!-- source: 190_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2452–2452 -->

## Frame Preemption Advance Register

The EMAC\_FPE\_ADV register contains the hold and release advance time.

Figure 30-210: EMAC\_FPE\_ADV Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-265: EMAC\_FPE\_ADV Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|--------------------|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:16 (R/W)        | RADV       | Release Advance. The EMAC_FPE_ADV.RADV field indicates the maximum time in nanoseconds that can elapse between issuing a RELEASE to the MAC and the MAC being ready to re- sume transmission of preemptable frames, in the absence of there being any express frames available for transmission. |
| 15:0 (R/W)         | HADV       | Hold Advance. The EMAC_FPE_ADV.HADV field indicates the maximum time in nanoseconds that can elapse between issuing a HOLD to the MAC, and the MAC ceasing to transmit any preemptable frame that is in the process of transmission or any preemptable frames that are queued for transmission.  |

## MTL Frame Preemption Control and Status Register

The EMAC\_FPE\_CTRLSTS register controls the operation of, and provides status for frame preemption (IEEE802.1Qbu/802.3br).

Figure 30-211: EMAC\_FPE\_CTRLSTS Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-266: EMAC\_FPE\_CTRLSTS Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|--------------------|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 28 (R/NW)          | HRS        | Hold/Release Status. The EMAC_FPE_CTRLSTS.HRS bit indicates whether a set-and-hold MAC opera- tion was last executed and the pMAC is in hold state or a set-and-release MAC opera- tion was last executed and the pMAC is in the release state.          |
| 15:8 (R/W)         | PEC        | Preemption Classification. When set (=1), the EMAC_FPE_CTRLSTS.PEC field indicates that the correspond- ing queue must be classified as preemptable, when '0' queue is classified as express.                                                            |
| 1:0 (R/W)          | AFSZ       | Additional Fragment Size. The EMAC_FPE_CTRLSTS.AFSZ field indicates, in units of 64 bytes, the mini- mum number of bytes over 64 bytes required in non-final fragments of preempted frames. The minimum non-final fragment size is (AFSZ +1) * 64 bytes. |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — Receive Queue Control Register

<!-- source: 196_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2463–2464 -->

## Receive Queue Control Register

The EMAC\_RQ0\_CTL register controls the receive arbitration and passing of received packets to the application.

Figure 30-216: EMAC\_RQ0\_CTL Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-271: EMAC\_RQ0\_CTL Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name      | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|--------------------|---------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 3 (R/W)            | RXQ_FRM_ARBIT | Receive Queue Packet Arbitration. When the EMAC_RQ0_CTL.RXQ_FRM_ARBIT bit is set, the EMAC module drives the packet data to the ARI interface such that the entire packet data of currently-select- ed queue is transmitted before switching to other queue. When EMAC_RQ0_CTL.RXQ_FRM_ARBIT = 0, the EMAC module drives the packet data to the ARI interface such that the following amount of data of currently- selected queue is transmitted before switching to other queue: - PBL amount of data or - Complete data of a packet The status and the time stamp are not a part of the PBL data. Therefore, the EMAC module drives the complete status (including time stamp status) during first PBL request for the packet (in store-and-forward mode) or the last PBL request for the packet (in threshold mode). |
| 3 (R/W)            |               | 0 Receive Queue Packet Arbitration is Disabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| 3 (R/W)            |               | 1 Receive Queue Packet Arbitration is Enabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

Table 30-271: EMAC\_RQ0\_CTL Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|--------------------|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 2:0 (R/W)          | RXQ_WEGT   | Receive Queue Weight. The EMAC_RQ0_CTL.RXQ_WEGT field indicates the weight assigned to the Rx queue 0. The field must be programmed with one value less than the required weight, that is, reset value of 0 indicates weight of 1, value of 1 indicates weight of 2, and so on. The weight is used as the number of continuous PBL or packets requests (depend- ing on the RXQ_FRM_ARBIT) allocated to the queue in one arbitration cycle. Note: The change in value of RXQ_WEGT takes effect only after the completion of current service round or when there is change from RAA=SP to RAA=WSP algorithm. This approach is taken so that there is smooth transition. For the RXQ_WEGT value to take effect at the start, the EMAC_RQ[n]_CTL registers must be programmed be- fore the EMAC_MTL_OPMODE register. |

Self-set to 1 on internal event.                                                                                                                                     |

The EMAC_RQ0_MSPKTOF_CNT.MISPKTCNT field indicates the number of pack- ets missed by the EMAC module because the application asserted EMAC_DMA[n]_RXCTL.RPF for this queue. This counter is incremented by 1 when the DMAdiscards the packet because of buffer unavailability. Access restriction applies. Clears on read. Self-set to 1 on internal event. | Missed Packet Counter. The EMAC_RQ0_MSPKTOF_CNT.MISPKTCNT field indicates the number of pack- ets missed by the EMAC module because the application asserted EMAC_DMA[n]_RXCTL.RPF for this queue. This counter is incremented by 1 when the DMAdiscards the packet because of buffer unavailability. Access restriction applies. Clears on read. Self-set to 1 on internal event. |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — Receive Queue 0 Operation Mode Register

<!-- source: 199_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2469–2472 -->

## Receive Queue 0 Operation Mode Register

The EMAC\_RQ0\_OPMODE register establishes the receive queue operating modes and command.

The RFA and RFD fields are not backward compatible with the RFA and RFD fields of 4.00a release.

Figure 30-219: EMAC\_RQ0\_OPMODE Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-274: EMAC\_RQ0\_OPMODE Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|--------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 25:20 (R/W)        | RQS        | Receive Queue Size. The EMAC_RQ0_OPMODE.RQS field indicates the size of the allocated receive queues in blocks of 256 bytes. The field is read-write only if the number of Rx queues more than one, the reset value is 0x0 and indicates size of 256 bytes. For example, the value of 0x0 = 256 bytes, 0x1 = 512 bytes and so on. So, program RQS [5:0] = 6'b001111 to allocate queue size of 4096 (4K) bytes. In general, the size of the queue = (RQS+1)*256 bytes. When the number of Rx queues is one, the field is read-only and the configured RX FIFO size in blocks of 256 bytes is reflected in the reset value. |

Table 30-274: EMAC\_RQ0\_OPMODE Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|--------------------|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 18:14 (R/W)        | RFD        | Threshold for Deactivating Flow Control. The EMAC_RQ0_OPMODE.RFD field indicates the threshold (fill-level of Rx queue) at which the flow control is deasserted after activation. It is valid in half-duplex and full-duplex mode). 0: Full minus 1 KB, that is, FULL 1 KB 1: Full minus 1.5 KB, that is, FULL 1.5 KB 2: Full minus 2 KB, that is, FULL 2 KB 3: Full minus 2.5 KB, that is, FULL 2.5 KB ... 30: Full minus 16 KB, that is, FULL 16 KB 31: Full minus 16.5 KB, that is, FULL 16.5 KB The deassertion is effective only after flow control is asserted. Note: The value must be programmed in such a way to make sure that the threshold is a positive number. When the EMAC_RQ0_OPMODE.EHFC bit is set (=1), these values are applicable on- ly when the Rx queue size determined by the EMAC_RQ0_OPMODE.RQS field, is equal to or greater than 4 KB. For a given queue size, the values ranges between 0 and the encoding for FULL minus (QSIZE - 0.5 KB) and all other values are illegal. Here the term FULL and QSIZE refers to the queue size determined by the EMAC_RQ0_OPMODE.RQS field. |
| 12:8 (R/W)         | RFA        | Threshold for Activating Flow Control. The EMAC_RQ0_OPMODE.RFA field indicates the threshold (fill-level of Rx queue) at which the flow control is activated. It is valid in half-duplex and full-duplex mode). For more information on encoding for this field, see RFD.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| 7 (R/W)            | EHFC       | Enable Hardware Flow Control. When the EMAC_RQ0_OPMODE.EHFC bit is set, the flow control signal operation, based on the fill-level of Rx queue, is enabled. When cleared (=0), the flow control op- eration is disabled. 0 Hardware Flow Control is Disabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| 7 (R/W)            | EHFC       | 1 Hardware Flow Control is Enabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

When the EMAC_RQ0_OPMODE.DIS_TCP_EF bit is set, the MAC does not drop the packets which only have the errors detected by the receive checksum offload en- gine. Such packets have errors only in the encapsulated payload. There are no errors (including FCS error) in the Ethernet packet received by the MAC. When EMAC_RQ0_OPMODE.DIS_TCP_EF = 0, all error packets are dropped if EMAC_RQ0_OPMODE.FEP = 0.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Disable Dropping of TCP/IP Checksum Error Packets. When EMAC_RQ0_OPMODE.RSF = 0, the Rx queue operates in the threshold (cut-through) mode, subject to the threshold specified by the EMAC_RQ0_OPMODE.RTC field.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Receive Queue Store and Forward. When the EMAC_RQ0_OPMODE.RSF bit is set, the EMAC module reads a packet from the Rx queue only after the complete packet has been written to it, ignoring the EMAC_RQ0_OPMODE.RTC field. When EMAC_RQ0_OPMODE.RSF = 0, the Rx queue operates in the threshold (cut-through) mode, subject to the threshold specified by the EMAC_RQ0_OPMODE.RTC field.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| 5 (R/W)            | RSF        | 0                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Receive Queue Store and Forward is Disabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| 5 (R/W)            | RSF        | 1                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Receive Queue Store and Forward is Enabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| 4 (R/W)            | FEP        | Forward Error Packets. When EMAC_RQ0_OPMODE.FEP = 0, the Rx queue drops packets with error status (CRC error, GMII_ER, watchdog timeout, or overflow). However, if the start byte (write) pointer of a packet is already transferred to the read controller side (in thresh- old mode), the packet is not dropped. When the EMAC_RQ0_OPMODE.FEP bit is set, all packets except the runt error packets are forwarded to the application or DMA. If the EMAC_RQ0_OPMODE.RSF = 1 and the Rx queue overflows when a partial packet is written, the packet is dropped irrespective of the setting of the EMAC_RQ0_OPMODE.FEP bit. However, if the EMAC_RQ0_OPMODE.RSF = 0 and the Rx queue overflows when a partial packet is written, a partial packet might be forwarded to the application or DMA. | Forward Error Packets. When EMAC_RQ0_OPMODE.FEP = 0, the Rx queue drops packets with error status (CRC error, GMII_ER, watchdog timeout, or overflow). However, if the start byte (write) pointer of a packet is already transferred to the read controller side (in thresh- old mode), the packet is not dropped. When the EMAC_RQ0_OPMODE.FEP bit is set, all packets except the runt error packets are forwarded to the application or DMA. If the EMAC_RQ0_OPMODE.RSF = 1 and the Rx queue overflows when a partial packet is written, the packet is dropped irrespective of the setting of the EMAC_RQ0_OPMODE.FEP bit. However, if the EMAC_RQ0_OPMODE.RSF = 0 and the Rx queue overflows when a partial packet is written, a partial packet might be forwarded to the application or DMA. |
| 4 (R/W)            | FEP        | 0                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Forward Error Packets is Disabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| 4 (R/W)            | FEP        | 1                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Forward Error Packets is Enabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

| 3 (R/W)            | FUP        | Forward Undersized Good Packets. When the EMAC_RQ0_OPMODE.FUP bit is set, the Rx queue forwards the under- sized good packets (packets with no error and length less than 64 bytes), including pad-bytes and CRC. When EMAC_RQ0_OPMODE.FUP = 0, the Rx queue drops all packets of less than 64 bytes, unless a packet is already transferred because of the lower value of Rx threshold, for example, RTC = 01.                                                                                                                                                                     |
| 1:0 (R/W)          | RTC        | 1 Forward Undersized Good Packets is Enabled Receive Queue Threshold Control. The EMAC_RQ0_OPMODE.RTC field indicates the threshold level of the MTL Rx queue (in bytes). The received packet is transferred to the application or DMAwhen the packet size within the MTL Rx queue is larger than the threshold. In addition, full packets with length less than the threshold are automatically transferred. The EMAC_RQ0_OPMODE.RTC field is valid only when EMAC_RQ0_OPMODE.RSF = 0. The EMAC_RQ0_OPMODE.RTC field is ignored when EMAC_RQ0_OPMODE.RSF = 1. 0 64 1 32 2 96 3 128 |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — Receive Queue n Control Register

<!-- source: 200_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2473–2474 -->

## Receive Queue n Control Register

The EMAC\_RQ[n]\_CTL register controls the receive arbitration and passing of received packets to the application.

Figure 30-220: EMAC\_RQ[n]\_CTL Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-275: EMAC\_RQ[n]\_CTL Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name      | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|--------------------|---------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 3 (R/W)            | RXQ_FRM_ARBIT | Receive Queue Packet Arbitration. When the EMAC_RQ[n]_CTL.RXQ_FRM_ARBIT bit is set, the EMAC module drives the packet data to the ARI interface such that the entire packet data of current- ly-selected queue is transmitted before switching to other queue. When EMAC_RQ[n]_CTL.RXQ_FRM_ARBIT = 0, the EMAC module drives the packet data to the ARI interface such that the following amount of data of currently- selected queue is transmitted before switching to other queue: - PBL amount of data or - Complete data of a packet The status and the time stamp are not a part of the PBL data. Therefore, the EMAC module drives the complete status (including time stamp status) during first PBL re- quest for the packet (in store-and-forward mode) or the last PBL request for the packet (in threshold mode). |
| 3 (R/W)            | RXQ_FRM_ARBIT | 0 Disabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| 3 (R/W)            | RXQ_FRM_ARBIT | 1 Enabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

Table 30-275: EMAC\_RQ[n]\_CTL Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|--------------------|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 2:0 (R/W)          | RXQ_WEGT   | Receive Queue Weight. The EMAC_RQ[n]_CTL.RXQ_WEGT field indicates the weight assigned to the Rx queue 0. The EMAC_RQ[n]_CTL.RXQ_WEGT field needs to be programmed with one value less than the required weight. For example, a reset value of 0 indicates a weight of 1, a value of 1 indicates weight of 2, and so on. The weight is used as the number of continuous PBL or packets requests (depending on the RXQ_FRM_AR- BIT) allocated to the queue in one arbitration cycle. Note: The change in value of RXQ_WEGT takes effect only after the completion of current service round or when there is change from RAA=SP to RAA=WSP algorithm. This approach is taken so that there is smooth transition. For the RXQ_WEGT value to take effect at the start, the EMAC_RQ[n]_CTL registers must be programmed be- fore the EMAC_MTL_OPMODE register. |

Self-set to 1 on internal event. 0 Overflow Not Detected                                                                                                      |

However, if the start byte (write) pointer of a packet is already transferred to the read controller side (in thresh- old mode), the packet is not dropped. When the EMAC_RQ[n]_OPMODE.FEP bit is set, all packets except the runt error packets are forwarded to the application or DMA. If the RSF bit is set and the Rx queue overflows when a partial packet is written, the packet is dropped irrespective of the setting of the EMAC_RQ[n]_OPMODE.FEP bit. However, if the RSF bit is reset and the Rx queue overflows when a partial packet is written, a partial packet might be forwarded to the application or DMA. 0 Disabled |
| 4 (R/W)            |            | 1 Enabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| 4 (R/W)            |            |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

Table 30-278: EMAC\_RQ[n]\_OPMODE Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
|--------------------|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 3 (R/W)            | FUP        | Forward Undersized Good Packets. When the EMAC_RQ[n]_OPMODE.FUP bit is set, the Rx queue forwards the un- dersized good packets (packets with no error and length less than 64 bytes), including pad-bytes and CRC. When EMAC_RQ[n]_OPMODE.FUP = 0, the Rx queue drops all packets of less than 64 bytes, unless a packet is already transferred because of the lower value of Rx threshold, for example, RTC = 01.                                                                                                                                |
| 1:0 (R/W)          | RTC        | 1 Enabled Receive Queue Threshold Control. The EMAC_RQ[n]_OPMODE.RTC field indicates the threshold level of the MTL Rx queue (in bytes). The received packet is transferred to the application or DMAwhen the packet size within the MTL Rx queue is larger than the threshold. In addition, full packets with length less than the threshold are automatically transferred. The EMAC_RQ[n]_OPMODE.RTC field is valid only when the RSF bit is zero. The EMAC_RQ[n]_OPMODE.RTC field is ignored when the RSF bit is set (=1). 0 64 1 32 2 96 3 128 |

## Receive Queue to DMA Channel Mapping Register 0

When set, the EMAC_RXQ_DMA_MAP0.Q3DDMACH bit indicates that the packets received in queue 3 are routed to a particular DMAchannel as decided in the MAC receiver based on the DMAchannel number programmed in the L3-L4 filter registers, or the Ethernet DA address. Note: The width of this field depends on the number of RX DMAchannels and not all the values might be valid in some configurations. For example, if the number of RX DMAchannels selected is 2, only 000 and 001 are valid, the others are reserved                                   |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — MTL Time Based Scheduling Control Register

<!-- source: 206_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2491–2492 -->

## MTL Time Based Scheduling Control Register

The EMAC\_TBS\_CTRL register controls the operation of Time-Based Scheduling (TBS).

Figure 30-226: EMAC\_TBS\_CTRL Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-281: EMAC\_TBS\_CTRL Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|--------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:8 (R/W)         | LEOS       | Launch Expiry Offset. The field contains the value in units of 256 nanoseconds that must be added to the launch time to compute the launch expiry time. The value is valid only when EMAC_TBS_CTRL.LEOV = 1. The max value, 999,999,999 ns, should be smaller than the CTR-1 value when ESTM mode is enabled, because this value is a modulo CTR value. |
| 6:4 (R/W)          | LEGOS      | Launch Expiry GSN Offset. The EMAC_TBS_CTRL.LEGOS field indicates the number GSN slots that must be added to the launch GSN to compute the launch expiry time. The value is valid only when EMAC_TBS_CTRL.LEOV = 1.                                                                                                                                     |
| 1 (R/W)            | LEOV       | Launch Expiry Offset Valid. When set (=1), the EMAC_TBS_CTRL.LEOV bit indicates that the EMAC_TBS_CTRL.LEOS field is valid. When not set, it indicates that the launch expiry offset is invalid and the MTL must not check for launch expiry time. LEOS Field is Invalid                                                                                |
| 1 (R/W)            | LEOV       | 0                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| 1 (R/W)            | LEOV       | 1 LEOS Field is Valid                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

Table 30-281: EMAC\_TBS\_CTRL Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|--------------------|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 0 (R/W)            | ESTM       | EST Offset Mode. When the EMAC_TBS_CTRL.ESTM bit is set, the launch time value used in time based scheduling is interpreted as an EST offset value and is added to the Base Time Register (BTR) of the current list. When cleared (=0), the launch time value is used as an absolute value that should be compared with the system time [39:8]. Disabled |
| 0 (R/W)            | ESTM       | 0                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| 0 (R/W)            | ESTM       | 1 Enabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

## Transmit Queue 0 Debug Register

The EMAC\_TQ0\_DBG register gives the debug status of various blocks related to the transmit queue.

Figure 30-227: EMAC\_TQ0\_DBG Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-282: EMAC\_TQ0\_DBG Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

# Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — Transmit Queue 0 ETS Status Register

## Transmit Queue 0 ETS Status Register

The EMAC\_TQ0\_ETS\_STAT register provides the average traffic transmitted in queue 0.

Figure 30-228: EMAC\_TQ0\_ETS\_STAT Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-283: EMAC\_TQ0\_ETS\_STAT Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|--------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 23:0 (R/NW)        | ABS        | Average Bits per Slot. The EMAC_TQ0_ETS_STAT.ABS field contains the average transmitted bits per slot. When the DCB operation is enabled for queue 0, this field is computed over every 10 million bit times slot (4 ms in 2500 Mbps; 10 ms in 1000 Mbps; 100 ms in 100 Mbps). The maximum value is 0x989680. |

## Transmit Queue 0 Operation Mode Register

The EMAC\_TQ0\_OPMODE register establishes the transmit queue operating modes and commands.

<!-- image -->

Transmit Queue Size

| 21:16 (R/W)        | TQS        | Transmit Queue Size. The EMAC_TQ0_OPMODE.TQS field indicates the size of the allocated transmit queues in blocks of 256 bytes. The field is read-write only if the number of Tx queues more than one, the reset value is 0x0 and indicates size of 256 bytes. For example, a value of 0x0 = 256 bytes, 0x1 = 512 bytes and so on. So, program TQS [5:0] = 6'b001111 to allocate queue size of 4096 (4K) bytes. In general, the size of the queue = (TQS+1)*256 bytes. When the number of Tx queues is one, the field is read-only and the configured TX FIFO size in blocks of 256 bytes is reflected in the reset value. | Transmit Queue Size. # Ethernet Media Access Controller (EMAC) — ADSP-SC59x EMAC Register Descriptions — Transmit Queue 0 IdleSlopeCredit, Quantum or Weights Register

<!-- source: 210_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_EMAC_ADSP-SC59x_EMAC_Regist.pdf | original pages 2498–2498 -->

## Transmit Queue 0 IdleSlopeCredit, Quantum or Weights Register

The EMAC\_TQ0\_QTMWGT register contains the quantum value for Deficit Weighted Round Robin (DWRR), weights for the Weighted Round Robin (WRR), and Weighted Fair Queuing (WFQ) for queue 0.

Figure 30-230: EMAC\_TQ0\_QTMWGT Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-285: EMAC\_TQ0\_QTMWGT Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|--------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 20:0 (R/W)         | ISCQW      | Quantum or Weights. When the DCB operation is enabled with DWRR algorithm for queue 0 traffic, the EMAC_TQ0_QTMWGT.ISCQW field contains the quantum value in bytes to be added to credit during every queue scanning cycle. The maximum value is 0x1312D0 bytes. When DCB operation is enabled with WFQalgorithm for queue 0 traffic, the EMAC_TQ0_QTMWGT.ISCQW field contains the weight for this queue. The maxi- mum value is 0x3FFF where weight of 0 indicates 100% bandwidth. Bits[20:14] must be written to zero. The higher the programmed weights lesser the bandwidth allocated for the particular transmit queue. This is because the weights are used to compute the packet finish time (weights * packet_size). Lesser the finish time, higher the probability of the packet getting scheduled first and using more bandwidth. When DCB operation or generic queuing operation is enabled with WRR algorithm for queue 0 traffic, this field contains the weight for this queue. The maximum value is 0x64. Bits [20:7] must be written to zero. |

## Transmit Queue 0 Underflow Packet Counter Register

The EMAC\_TQ0\_URFL register contains the counter for packets aborted because of transmit queue underflow and packets missed because of receive queue packet flush.

Figure 30-231: EMAC\_TQ0\_URFL Register Diagram

<!-- image -->

Table 30-286: EMAC\_TQ0\_URFL Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|--------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 11 (R/NW)          | UFCNTOVF   | Overflow Bit for Underflow Packet Counter. The EMAC_TQ0_URFL.UFCNTOVF bit is set every time the Tx queue Underflow Packet Counter field overflows, that is, it has crossed the maximum count. In such a scenario, the overflow packet counter is reset to all-zeros and the EMAC_TQ0_URFL.UFCNTOVF bit indicates that the rollover happened. Access restriction applies. Clears on read. Self-set to 1 on internal event. | Overflow Bit for Underflow Packet Counter. The EMAC_TQ0_URFL.UFCNTOVF bit is set every time the Tx queue Underflow Packet Counter field overflows, that is, it has crossed the maximum count. In such a scenario, the overflow packet counter is reset to all-zeros and the EMAC_TQ0_URFL.UFCNTOVF bit indicates that the rollover happened. Access restriction applies. Clears on read. Self-set to 1 on internal event. |
| 10:0 (R/NW)        | UFFRMCNT   | Underflow Packet Counter. The EMAC_TQ0_URFL.UFFRMCNT field indicates the number of packets aborted by the controller because of Tx queue underflow. This counter is incremented each time the MAC aborts outgoing packet because of underflow. Access restriction applies. Clears on read. Self-set to 1 on internal event.                                                                                               | Underflow Packet Counter. The EMAC_TQ0_URFL.UFFRMCNT field indicates the number of packets aborted by the controller because of Tx queue underflow. This counter is incremented each time the MAC aborts outgoing packet because of underflow. Access restriction applies. Clears on read. Self-set to 1 on internal event.                                                                                               |
